- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request

1	# Zeo 0.2.2 — Altium-Parity Board Creation Roadmap
2	
3	## Goal
4	
5	Bring Zeo's board creation to Altium-caliber quality for a **solo designer**.
6	Team / lifecycle / supplier-sync features are explicitly out of scope. The focus
7	is the act of designing, routing, verifying, and outputting one (or a small set
8	of) boards.
9	
10	## Scope cuts (deferred or declined)
11	
12	- Component lifecycle (preliminary / released / obsolete state machines)
13	- Vault / shared org-wide library (Altium 365 equivalents)
14	- ActiveBOM / live supplier sync (Zeo agent's pcbparts.dev MCP covers one-shot
15	  lookups; live BOM not in scope)
16	- Harness / cable design
17	- ECO / changeset audit trail (current sch ↔ pcb update is sufficient for solo)
18	- Team review workflows
19	- IPC-2581 / ODB++ (Gerber + STEP cover solo fab)
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Audit findings (2026-05-15)
24	
25	Four code audits reshaped the scope. Summary:
26	
27	1. **Variants are fully implemented**, including most of the UI. C2 collapses
28	   from "build feature" to a small set of targeted UX gap fixes.
29	2. **Constraint engine is mature**, evaluated per-segment by PNS already.
30	   A1 is a 6-ticket "extend" not a refactor.
31	3. **Transline calculators exist** for microstrip/stripline/etc. A3 is mostly
32	   UX wiring.
33	4. **Real-time DRC is feasible** for 5 high-leverage constraints at
34	   ~1.2 ms/segment total cost. Length/skew defer to commit-time.
35	5. **PnS router gaps don't justify 0.2.2 work.** Entire C3 defers to 0.3+.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## Trunk realization
40	
41	Constraints, stackup, and signal integrity are one tightly coupled trio. They
42	are mostly **already built** in KiCad. The 0.2.2 trunk work is **connecting**
43	them, not building them.
44	
45	---
46	
47	## Phase A — Trunk (6 concrete tickets)
48	
49	### A1. Add `IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT` (enum + parser)
50	
51	Touch points:
52	
53	- `pcbnew/drc/drc_rule.h:85–86` — add enum value after `MAX_UNCOUPLED_CONSTRAINT`
54	- `common/drc_rules.keywords` (~line 28, alphabetical) — add `impedance_target`
55	- `pcbnew/drc/drc_rule_parser.cpp:499–558` — add parse case mirroring
56	  `LENGTH_CONSTRAINT`; uses `MINOPTMAX<int>` triple (milli-ohms internal units)
57	- `include/drc_item.h` — add `DRCE_IMPEDANCE_MISMATCH` error code
58	
59	**Effort:** ~1 day. **Pattern from:** `case T_length: c.m_Type = LENGTH_CONSTRAINT;`
60	
61	### A2. Create `DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_IMPEDANCE`
62	
63	Touch points:
64	
65	- **New file:** `pcbnew/drc/drc_test_provider_impedance.cpp/.h`
66	- Iterates `PCB_TRACK_T` / `PCB_ARC_T` / `PCB_VIA_T` items via
67	  `forEachGeometryItem()` — pattern from
68	  `drc_test_provider_matched_length.cpp:374–400`
69	- Per-track: get adjacent dielectric from `BOARD_STACKUP` via
70	  `GetLayerDistance()` and dielectric items, then call `MICROSTRIP` or
71	  `STRIPLINE` `Analyse()` to get computed Z₀
72	- Compare against constraint's `MINOPTMAX<int>`; emit `DRC_ITEM` on violation
73	- Auto-registers via `DRC_REGISTER_TEST_PROVIDER<>` macro at file scope
74	
75	**Caching:** mirror `m_netclassClearances` pattern in `drc_engine.h:374–398` —
76	add `m_impedanceCache` keyed by `{netcode, layer, width}`.
77	
78	**Effort:** ~2–3 days. **Depends on:** A1.
79	
80	### A3. Impedance in track properties dialog
81	
82	Touch points:
83	
84	- `pcbnew/dialogs/dialog_track_via_size.h/.cpp` — add read-only `wxTextCtrl`
85	  for computed Z₀; populate on width/layer/net change
86	
87	**Effort:** ~1 day. **Depends on:** A2.
88	
89	### A4. Impedance in PNS router status display
90	
91	Touch points:
92	
93	- `pcbnew/router/router_tool.cpp:2128, 2690` — append `Z₀ = X.X Ω (target Y.Y Ω)`
94	  to existing status messaging via `statusItem->AppendMessage()`
95	
96	**Effort:** ~0.5 day. **Depends on:** A2.
97	
98	### A5. Impedance column in Net Inspector
99	
100	Touch points:
101	
102	- `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel.h:308–321` — add `COLUMN_AVG_IMPEDANCE`
103	  before `COLUMN_LAST_STATIC_COL`
104	- `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel_data_model.h` — add `m_avg_impedance`
105	  to LIST_ITEM; add `GetValue()` case
106	- `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel.cpp::buildNetsList()` — compute
107	  per-net average Z₀ from all tracks
108	
109	**Effort:** ~1.5 days. **Depends on:** A2.
110	
111	### A6. Variant condition syntax in rule expressions
112	
113	Touch points:
114	
115	- `pcbnew/pcbexpr_evaluator.cpp` — add `variantIs(name)` function reading
116	  `BOARD::GetCurrentVariant()` (already exists at `board.h:427`,
117	  member `m_currentVariant` at `board.h:1681`)
118	- `pcbnew/pcbexpr_functions.cpp` — register `variantIs` in expression
119	  function registry
120	
121	Lets rule authors write `(condition "variantIs('assembly_v2')")`.
122	
123	**Effort:** ~1 day. **Depends on:** none (parallelizable).
124	
125	**Phase A total: 6 tickets, ~7–8 days of work.**
126	
127	---
128	
129	## Phase B — UX polish on the trunk
130	
131	### B1. Real-time DRC during routing (5 constraints + spike)
132	
133	Per the audit, 5 constraints are feasible per-segment with a total budget of
134	**~1.2 ms/segment** (well under the 16 ms/frame budget):
135	
136	| Constraint | Per-segment cost | Implementation |
137	|------------|------------------|----------------|
138	| `TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.05 ms | Single property check |
139	| `VIA_DIAMETER_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.05 ms | Single property check |
140	| `TRACK_ANGLE_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.2 ms | Local neighbor query |
141	| `DISALLOW_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.5 ms | RTree spatial query (cached) |
142	| `VIA_COUNT_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.3 ms | Active-path via count |
143	
144	Length / skew defer to commit-time (audit measured ~50–100 ms/eval due to
145	cross-board graph walks — infeasible per-segment).
146	
147	**Spike plan (B1a):** Implement `TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT` only first,
148	measure actual latency. Touch points:
149	
150	- `pcbnew/router/pns_node.h:72–81` — extend `PNS::CONSTRAINT` struct with
151	  `wxString m_ViolationDetail`
152	- `pcbnew/router/pns_kicad_iface.cpp:434–684` —
153	  `PNS_PCBNEW_RULE_RESOLVER::QueryConstraint()` evaluates `TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT`
154	  and populates detail string
155	- `pcbnew/router/router_tool.cpp:2120–2135` — replace generic "Track violates
156	  DRC" with per-rule violation list
157	- `pcbnew/router/router_status_view_item.cpp::ViewDraw()` — render multiline
158	  detail
159	
160	**Success criterion:** <2 ms/segment for the full 5-constraint set.
161	If spike measures >3 ms, batch via existing `DRC_CLEARANCE_BATCH` pattern
162	or add incremental RTree maintenance.
163	
164	**Effort:** 2 tickets (spike + remaining 4 constraints). **Depends on:** A1.
165	
166	### B2. Schematic-side ergonomics for existing diff-pair declaration
167	
168	**Decision (2026-05-15):** Keep the existing diff-pair declaration mechanism
169	(`PROJECT_FILE::GetCrossBoardDiffPairs()` + `NETCLASS` diff-pair properties).
170	Don't invent new s-expr syntax. The 0.2.2 work is making the existing
171	mechanism reachable from the schematic UI more naturally — declare a
172	diff pair from the schematic context menu, persist via the existing
173	project-level mechanism.
174	
175	Length-match groups deferred to 0.3 along with C3.
176	
177	**Effort:** 1 ticket. **Depends on:** A1.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## Phase C — Extensions
182	
183	### C1. 3D MCAD round-trip
184	
185	STEP **import** + "mechanical source" tracking. STEP export already works.
186	
187	- STEP reader in `pcbnew/pcb_io/`
188	- Flag features as "derived from external STEP"
189	- Diff workflow: re-import → show changed mounting holes / outline → apply
190	
191	**Effort:** 2–3 tickets. **Depends on:** none (independent).
192	
193	### C2. Variants — targeted UX polish (re-scoped after audit)
194	
195	Variants are fully working end-to-end with most UI built. Audit identified
196	the following gaps:
197	
198	| Gap | Severity | Touch point |
199	|-----|----------|-------------|
200	| **Implicit field override in properties dialogs** (no UI indication that editing a field in a variant context creates an override) | MAJOR | `eeschema/dialogs/dialog_symbol_properties.cpp:408–796`, `pcbnew/dialogs/dialog_footprint_properties.cpp:255–672` |
201	| **No variant selector in BOM export dialog** (CLI only) | MAJOR | `eeschema/dialogs/dialog_bom.cpp` — add `m_choiceVariant` dropdown |
202	| **No variant-diff viewer** (field-level only for 0.2.2; visual canvas diff deferred to 0.2.3) | MAJOR | New dialog; iterate `VARIANT::GetFieldOverrides()` between two variants |
203	| **No active-variant status indicator outside toolbar** | Minor | Status bar widget reading `BOARD::GetCurrentVariant()` / sch equivalent |
204	| **DRC doesn't validate variant consistency** (DNP in one variant only) | Partial | `pcbnew/drc/drc_test_provider_schematic_parity.cpp:180` — extend variant-aware check |
205	| **Buried Tools > Variants menu** | Minor | `eeschema/menubar.cpp` — promote variant menu visibility |
206	| **No help / discoverability** | Minor | Tooltips + docs |
207	
208	**Effort:** 3–4 tickets total:
209	
210	- C2a: Explicit override indicator in properties dialogs (biggest)
211	- C2b: BOM export variant selector UI
212	- C2c: Variant-diff viewer (field-level table only; visual canvas highlighting deferred to 0.2.3)
213	- C2d: Variant consistency in DRC + minor discoverability polish
214	
215	**Depends on:** none for most; C2d depends on A1 if we add variant-scoped
216	rules.
217	
218	### C3. PnS router polish — **defer all to 0.3+**
219	
220	Per audit verdict:
221	
222	| Gap | Verdict | Rationale |
223	|-----|---------|-----------|
224	| Length-match groups | Defer to 0.3 | 2–3 tickets, requires upfront UI/data-model design. Single-net tune sufficient for 0.2.2. |
225	| Soft rules / preference engine | **Drop** | 4–6 weeks; architectural change; low user demand |
226	| Native autorouter | Defer to 0.3+ | Freerouting works; 4–8 weeks for native |
227	| Hugging mode | Defer to 0.3 | Walkaround is good enough |
228	
229	C3 is **out of 0.2.2** entirely.
230	
231	### C4. Stackup per-region (rigid-flex) — **deferred to 0.2.3**
232	
233	**Decision (2026-05-15):** Rigid-flex out of 0.2.2 scope. Extend
234	`BOARD_STACKUP` with named regions in 0.2.3. A2 design should keep the
235	data model open to per-region stackup but not implement it yet.
236	
237	**Effort:** 3–4 tickets (in 0.2.3).
238	
239	---
240	
241	## Phase ordering
242	
243	```
244	A1 (impedance enum/parser)
245	 ├─► A2 (impedance test provider)
246	 │    ├─► A3 (track props dialog)
247	 │    ├─► A4 (PNS status display)
248	 │    └─► A5 (Net Inspector column)
249	 └─► (parallel) A6 (variant condition syntax)
250	
251	A1/A2 ──► B1a (TRACK_WIDTH spike)
252	          └─► B1b (remaining 4 constraints)
253	A1 ──► B2 (sch-side signal classes)
254	
255	(independent)
256	C1 (STEP import)
257	C2a–C2d (variants UX polish)
258	C4 (rigid-flex regions; depends on A2 if pursued)
259	```
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Linear ticket plan — Zeo 0.2.2
264	
265	| Phase | Tickets | Total effort |
266	|-------|---------|--------------|
267	| A1 enum+parser | 1 | ~1 d |
268	| A2 test provider | 1 | ~3 d |
269	| A3 track props | 1 | ~1 d |
270	| A4 PNS status | 1 | ~0.5 d |
271	| A5 net inspector | 1 | ~1.5 d |
272	| A6 variant condition | 1 | ~1 d |
273	| B1a real-time DRC spike | 1 | ~2 d |
274	| B1b real-time DRC rollout | 1 | ~3 d |
275	| B2 sch diff-pair ergonomics | 1 | ~1.5 d |
276	| C1 STEP import | 2–3 | ~5 d |
277	| C2a override indicator | 1 | ~1.5 d |
278	| C2b BOM variant UI | 1 | ~1 d |
279	| C2c variant-diff (field table only) | 1 | ~2 d |
280	| C2d variant DRC + polish | 1 | ~2 d |
281	| **Total** | **13–14 tickets** | **~25 d** |
282	
283	C3 (PnS), C4 (rigid-flex), C2c visual diff → 0.2.3.
284	Phase D (DSL integration) → 0.2.4.
285	
286	C3 (PnS polish) — entirely out of 0.2.2.
287	
288	---
289	
290	---
291	
292	## Version map
293	
294	| Release | Theme | Phases |
295	|---------|-------|--------|
296	| **0.2.2** | Altium-parity board creation (trunk + UX) | A, B, C (excl. C4) |
297	| **0.2.3** | Polish + extensions | C4 rigid-flex, visual variant diff, C3 PnS polish |
298	| **0.2.4** | DSL integration (Zener-based) | Phase D (all of it) |
299	
300	The version split reflects a deliberate **features-first** ordering. KiCad's
301	data model is the source of truth; the DSL is a view of it. Extending the
302	data model (Phase A) before the DSL (Phase D) avoids circular dependencies
303	and double-work. Forking `diodeinc/pcb` and extending Zener to cover our
304	extensions (impedance, variants, SI) is its own multi-week effort that
305	sits naturally after the underlying data model is solid.
306	
307	A lightweight check during 0.2.2 / 0.2.3 ticket work: for each feature
308	landed, note whether it'd encode naturally in Zener. If yes, ship.
309	If no, flag in the ticket for 0.2.4 consideration. That's a checklist
310	item, not a workstream.
311	
312	---
313	
314	## 0.2.3 backlog (deferred from 0.2.2)
315	
316	- **C4 — Stackup per-region / rigid-flex** (3–4 tickets)
317	- **B2 visual signal-class declaration** beyond the existing mechanism (if
318	  ergonomics work in 0.2.2 proves the basic flow needs richer syntax)
319	- **C2c visual variant diff** — highlight differences on the schematic / PCB
320	  canvas (field-level table ships in 0.2.2)
321	- **C3 — PnS router polish** (length-match groups, hugging, native autorouter)
322	- **Web dashboard / privacy panel / variants-in-CLI** from MOON-1407 Phase 2
323	
324	---
325	
326	## 0.2.4 — Phase D: DSL integration (Zener via forked diodeinc/pcb)
327	
328	### Why
329	
330	Current agent → board flow is `agent → IPC tool call → modify board`. Each
331	edit is an individual IPC roundtrip; agent has no holistic representation
332	of the design. Switching to `agent → write DSL → compile DSL → board` gives:
333	
334	- A single source of truth the agent can read/diff in one shot
335	- Fast compile time (Starlark-based, can re-run on every save)
336	- Constraint declarations live with the design (not scattered in rules)
337	- A natural place for project settings (no more "edit this dialog, edit
338	  that file")
339	- Round-trip with visual editor: agent can also *read* what a human just
340	  drew
341	
342	By 0.2.4 the underlying data model (impedance constraints, variant
343	scoping, stackup integration, real-time DRC, sch-side diff pairs) lands
344	in 0.2.2/0.2.3 — Phase D is then a clean encoding problem rather than a
345	co-design problem.
346	
347	### Prior art
348	
349	- **zeo1** was a full Rust rebuild around this concept; too big to land.
350	  Its `.zeo` language design (in `zeo1/plans/ref/zeo-language-spec.md`)
351	  is explicitly modeled on Zener.
352	- **diodeinc/pcb** (Zener language) is the closest external thing, with
353	  reusable Cargo crates: `pcb-zen` (compiler), `pcb-zen-core` (IR),
354	  `pcb-sch` (schematic IR), `pcb-kicad` (KiCad output), `pcb-mcp`
355	  (agent bridge), `pcb-starlark-lsp` (LSP).
356	
357	### Architecture
358	
359	```
360	C++ Zeo (eeschema, pcbnew, agent)
361	   ◄──IPC──►  kicad-api-rs (existing "zeo-rust"; needs KiCad 10 refresh)
362	              zeo-zen-bridge (NEW C ABI crate)
363	                 depends on (forked):
364	                 - pcb-zen, pcb-zen-core  (compile)
365	                 - pcb-sch                (schematic IR)
366	                 - pcb-kicad              (KiCad output)
367	                 - pcb-starlark-lsp       (LSP for editor)
368	                 - pcb-mcp                (agent integration path)
369	                 with Zeo extensions for:
370	                 - impedance targets       (from 0.2.2 A1)
371	                 - variant scoping         (from 0.2.2 A6)
372	                 - sch-side diff pairs     (from 0.2.2 B2)
373	                 - rigid-flex regions      (from 0.2.3 C4, if landed)
374	```
375	
376	The existing `zeo-rust` (kicad-api-rs) stays separate — it's the
377	live-session IPC. The new `zeo-zen-bridge` is the DSL compile/decompile
378	engine.
379	
380	### Phase D scope (0.2.4)
381	
382	**Foundation (~9 d, 6 tickets):**
383	
384	- **D1.** Update `zeo-rust` (kicad-api-rs) to current KiCad 10 protobuf
385	  schema. The bindings have drifted; refresh codegen against
386	  `api/proto/`. ~1.5 d.
387	- **D2.** Fork `diodeinc/pcb`; create `zeo-zen-bridge` Cargo crate;
388	  vendor `pcb-zen`, `pcb-zen-core`, `pcb-sch`, `pcb-kicad`. ~1 d.
389	- **D3.** Expose C ABI:
390	  `int zen_compile(const char* zen_path, const char* kicad_sch_out)` →
391	  invokes `pcb-zen::compile` then `pcb-kicad::emit`. ~3 d.
392	- **D4.** CMake wiring: build `zeo-zen-bridge` as part of the Zeo build;
393	  expose to `agent/` and `kicad/` kifaces. ~1 d.
394	- **D5.** CLI command in Zeo: `Zeo compile path/to/foo.zen` produces
395	  `.kicad_sch` next to it. ~1 d.
396	- **D6.** End-to-end smoke test: blinky example (from
397	  `diodeinc/pcb/examples/blinky.zen`) compiles cleanly, opens in Zeo

# Zeo 0.2.2 — Altium-Parity Board Creation Roadmap

## Goal

Bring Zeo's board creation to Altium-caliber quality for a **solo designer**.
Team / lifecycle / supplier-sync features are explicitly out of scope. The focus
is the act of designing, routing, verifying, and outputting one (or a small set
of) boards.

## Scope cuts (deferred or declined)

- Component lifecycle (preliminary / released / obsolete state machines)
- Vault / shared org-wide library (Altium 365 equivalents)
- ActiveBOM / live supplier sync (Zeo agent's pcbparts.dev MCP covers one-shot
  lookups; live BOM not in scope)
- Harness / cable design
- ECO / changeset audit trail (current sch ↔ pcb update is sufficient for solo)
- Team review workflows
- IPC-2581 / ODB++ (Gerber + STEP cover solo fab)

---

## Audit findings (2026-05-15)

Four code audits reshaped the scope. Summary:

1. **Variants are fully implemented**, including most of the UI. C2 collapses
   from "build feature" to a small set of targeted UX gap fixes.
2. **Constraint engine is mature**, evaluated per-segment by PNS already.
   A1 is a 6-ticket "extend" not a refactor.
3. **Transline calculators exist** for microstrip/stripline/etc. A3 is mostly
   UX wiring.
4. **Real-time DRC is feasible** for 5 high-leverage constraints at
   ~1.2 ms/segment total cost. Length/skew defer to commit-time.
5. **PnS router gaps don't justify 0.2.2 work.** Entire C3 defers to 0.3+.

---

## Trunk realization

Constraints, stackup, and signal integrity are one tightly coupled trio. They
are mostly **already built** in KiCad. The 0.2.2 trunk work is **connecting**
them, not building them.

---

## Phase A — Trunk (6 concrete tickets)

### A1. Add `IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT` (enum + parser)

Touch points:

- `pcbnew/drc/drc_rule.h:85–86` — add enum value after `MAX_UNCOUPLED_CONSTRAINT`
- `common/drc_rules.keywords` (~line 28, alphabetical) — add `impedance_target`
- `pcbnew/drc/drc_rule_parser.cpp:499–558` — add parse case mirroring
  `LENGTH_CONSTRAINT`; uses `MINOPTMAX<int>` triple (milli-ohms internal units)
- `include/drc_item.h` — add `DRCE_IMPEDANCE_MISMATCH` error code

**Effort:** ~1 day. **Pattern from:** `case T_length: c.m_Type = LENGTH_CONSTRAINT;`

### A2. Create `DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_IMPEDANCE`

Touch points:

- **New file:** `pcbnew/drc/drc_test_provider_impedance.cpp/.h`
- Iterates `PCB_TRACK_T` / `PCB_ARC_T` / `PCB_VIA_T` items via
  `forEachGeometryItem()` — pattern from
  `drc_test_provider_matched_length.cpp:374–400`
- Per-track: get adjacent dielectric from `BOARD_STACKUP` via
  `GetLayerDistance()` and dielectric items, then call `MICROSTRIP` or
  `STRIPLINE` `Analyse()` to get computed Z₀
- Compare against constraint's `MINOPTMAX<int>`; emit `DRC_ITEM` on violation
- Auto-registers via `DRC_REGISTER_TEST_PROVIDER<>` macro at file scope

**Caching:** mirror `m_netclassClearances` pattern in `drc_engine.h:374–398` —
add `m_impedanceCache` keyed by `{netcode, layer, width}`.

**Effort:** ~2–3 days. **Depends on:** A1.

### A3. Impedance in track properties dialog

Touch points:

- `pcbnew/dialogs/dialog_track_via_size.h/.cpp` — add read-only `wxTextCtrl`
  for computed Z₀; populate on width/layer/net change

**Effort:** ~1 day. **Depends on:** A2.

### A4. Impedance in PNS router status display

Touch points:

- `pcbnew/router/router_tool.cpp:2128, 2690` — append `Z₀ = X.X Ω (target Y.Y Ω)`
  to existing status messaging via `statusItem->AppendMessage()`

**Effort:** ~0.5 day. **Depends on:** A2.

### A5. Impedance column in Net Inspector

Touch points:

- `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel.h:308–321` — add `COLUMN_AVG_IMPEDANCE`
  before `COLUMN_LAST_STATIC_COL`
- `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel_data_model.h` — add `m_avg_impedance`
  to LIST_ITEM; add `GetValue()` case
- `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel.cpp::buildNetsList()` — compute
  per-net average Z₀ from all tracks

**Effort:** ~1.5 days. **Depends on:** A2.

### A6. Variant condition syntax in rule expressions

Touch points:

- `pcbnew/pcbexpr_evaluator.cpp` — add `variantIs(name)` function reading
  `BOARD::GetCurrentVariant()` (already exists at `board.h:427`,
  member `m_currentVariant` at `board.h:1681`)
- `pcbnew/pcbexpr_functions.cpp` — register `variantIs` in expression
  function registry

Lets rule authors write `(condition "variantIs('assembly_v2')")`.

**Effort:** ~1 day. **Depends on:** none (parallelizable).

**Phase A total: 6 tickets, ~7–8 days of work.**

---

## Phase B — UX polish on the trunk

### B1. Real-time DRC during routing (5 constraints + spike)

Per the audit, 5 constraints are feasible per-segment with a total budget of
**~1.2 ms/segment** (well under the 16 ms/frame budget):

| Constraint | Per-segment cost | Implementation |
|------------|------------------|----------------|
| `TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.05 ms | Single property check |
| `VIA_DIAMETER_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.05 ms | Single property check |
| `TRACK_ANGLE_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.2 ms | Local neighbor query |
| `DISALLOW_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.5 ms | RTree spatial query (cached) |
| `VIA_COUNT_CONSTRAINT` | ~0.3 ms | Active-path via count |

Length / skew defer to commit-time (audit measured ~50–100 ms/eval due to
cross-board graph walks — infeasible per-segment).

**Spike plan (B1a):** Implement `TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT` only first,
measure actual latency. Touch points:

- `pcbnew/router/pns_node.h:72–81` — extend `PNS::CONSTRAINT` struct with
  `wxString m_ViolationDetail`
- `pcbnew/router/pns_kicad_iface.cpp:434–684` —
  `PNS_PCBNEW_RULE_RESOLVER::QueryConstraint()` evaluates `TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT`
  and populates detail string
- `pcbnew/router/router_tool.cpp:2120–2135` — replace generic "Track violates
  DRC" with per-rule violation list
- `pcbnew/router/router_status_view_item.cpp::ViewDraw()` — render multiline
  detail

**Success criterion:** <2 ms/segment for the full 5-constraint set.
If spike measures >3 ms, batch via existing `DRC_CLEARANCE_BATCH` pattern
or add incremental RTree maintenance.

**Effort:** 2 tickets (spike + remaining 4 constraints). **Depends on:** A1.

### B2. Schematic-side ergonomics for existing diff-pair declaration

**Decision (2026-05-15):** Keep the existing diff-pair declaration mechanism
(`PROJECT_FILE::GetCrossBoardDiffPairs()` + `NETCLASS` diff-pair properties).
Don't invent new s-expr syntax. The 0.2.2 work is making the existing
mechanism reachable from the schematic UI more naturally — declare a
diff pair from the schematic context menu, persist via the existing
project-level mechanism.

Length-match groups deferred to 0.3 along with C3.

**Effort:** 1 ticket. **Depends on:** A1.

---

## Phase C — Extensions

### C1. 3D MCAD round-trip

STEP **import** + "mechanical source" tracking. STEP export already works.

- STEP reader in `pcbnew/pcb_io/`
- Flag features as "derived from external STEP"
- Diff workflow: re-import → show changed mounting holes / outline → apply

**Effort:** 2–3 tickets. **Depends on:** none (independent).

### C2. Variants — targeted UX polish (re-scoped after audit)

Variants are fully working end-to-end with most UI built. Audit identified
the following gaps:

| Gap | Severity | Touch point |
|-----|----------|-------------|
| **Implicit field override in properties dialogs** (no UI indication that editing a field in a variant context creates an override) | MAJOR | `eeschema/dialogs/dialog_symbol_properties.cpp:408–796`, `pcbnew/dialogs/dialog_footprint_properties.cpp:255–672` |
| **No variant selector in BOM export dialog** (CLI only) | MAJOR | `eeschema/dialogs/dialog_bom.cpp` — add `m_choiceVariant` dropdown |
| **No variant-diff viewer** (field-level only for 0.2.2; visual canvas diff deferred to 0.2.3) | MAJOR | New dialog; iterate `VARIANT::GetFieldOverrides()` between two variants |
| **No active-variant status indicator outside toolbar** | Minor | Status bar widget reading `BOARD::GetCurrentVariant()` / sch equivalent |
| **DRC doesn't validate variant consistency** (DNP in one variant only) | Partial | `pcbnew/drc/drc_test_provider_schematic_parity.cpp:180` — extend variant-aware check |
| **Buried Tools > Variants menu** | Minor | `eeschema/menubar.cpp` — promote variant menu visibility |
| **No help / discoverability** | Minor | Tooltips + docs |

**Effort:** 3–4 tickets total:

- C2a: Explicit override indicator in properties dialogs (biggest)
- C2b: BOM export variant selector UI
- C2c: Variant-diff viewer (field-level table only; visual canvas highlighting deferred to 0.2.3)
- C2d: Variant consistency in DRC + minor discoverability polish

**Depends on:** none for most; C2d depends on A1 if we add variant-scoped
rules.

### C3. PnS router polish — **defer all to 0.3+**

Per audit verdict:

| Gap | Verdict | Rationale |
|-----|---------|-----------|
| Length-match groups | Defer to 0.3 | 2–3 tickets, requires upfront UI/data-model design. Single-net tune sufficient for 0.2.2. |
| Soft rules / preference engine | **Drop** | 4–6 weeks; architectural change; low user demand |
| Native autorouter | Defer to 0.3+ | Freerouting works; 4–8 weeks for native |
| Hugging mode | Defer to 0.3 | Walkaround is good enough |

C3 is **out of 0.2.2** entirely.

### C4. Stackup per-region (rigid-flex) — **deferred to 0.2.3**

**Decision (2026-05-15):** Rigid-flex out of 0.2.2 scope. Extend
`BOARD_STACKUP` with named regions in 0.2.3. A2 design should keep the
data model open to per-region stackup but not implement it yet.

**Effort:** 3–4 tickets (in 0.2.3).

---

## Phase ordering

```
A1 (impedance enum/parser)
 ├─► A2 (impedance test provider)
 │    ├─► A3 (track props dialog)
 │    ├─► A4 (PNS status display)
 │    └─► A5 (Net Inspector column)
 └─► (parallel) A6 (variant condition syntax)

A1/A2 ──► B1a (TRACK_WIDTH spike)
          └─► B1b (remaining 4 constraints)
A1 ──► B2 (sch-side signal classes)

(independent)
C1 (STEP import)
C2a–C2d (variants UX polish)
C4 (rigid-flex regions; depends on A2 if pursued)
```

---

## Linear ticket plan — Zeo 0.2.2

| Phase | Tickets | Total effort |
|-------|---------|--------------|
| A1 enum+parser | 1 | ~1 d |
| A2 test provider | 1 | ~3 d |
| A3 track props | 1 | ~1 d |
| A4 PNS status | 1 | ~0.5 d |
| A5 net inspector | 1 | ~1.5 d |
| A6 variant condition | 1 | ~1 d |
| B1a real-time DRC spike | 1 | ~2 d |
| B1b real-time DRC rollout | 1 | ~3 d |
| B2 sch diff-pair ergonomics | 1 | ~1.5 d |
| C1 STEP import | 2–3 | ~5 d |
| C2a override indicator | 1 | ~1.5 d |
| C2b BOM variant UI | 1 | ~1 d |
| C2c variant-diff (field table only) | 1 | ~2 d |
| C2d variant DRC + polish | 1 | ~2 d |
| **Total** | **13–14 tickets** | **~25 d** |

C3 (PnS), C4 (rigid-flex), C2c visual diff → 0.2.3.
Phase D (DSL integration) → 0.2.4.

C3 (PnS polish) — entirely out of 0.2.2.

---

---

## Version map

| Release | Theme | Phases |
|---------|-------|--------|
| **0.2.2** | Altium-parity board creation (trunk + UX) | A, B, C (excl. C4) |
| **0.2.3** | Polish + extensions | C4 rigid-flex, visual variant diff, C3 PnS polish |
| **0.2.4** | DSL integration (Zener-based) | Phase D (all of it) |

The version split reflects a deliberate **features-first** ordering. KiCad's
data model is the source of truth; the DSL is a view of it. Extending the
data model (Phase A) before the DSL (Phase D) avoids circular dependencies
and double-work. Forking `diodeinc/pcb` and extending Zener to cover our
extensions (impedance, variants, SI) is its own multi-week effort that
sits naturally after the underlying data model is solid.

A lightweight check during 0.2.2 / 0.2.3 ticket work: for each feature
landed, note whether it'd encode naturally in Zener. If yes, ship.
If no, flag in the ticket for 0.2.4 consideration. That's a checklist
item, not a workstream.

---

## 0.2.3 backlog (deferred from 0.2.2)

- **C4 — Stackup per-region / rigid-flex** (3–4 tickets)
- **B2 visual signal-class declaration** beyond the existing mechanism (if
  ergonomics work in 0.2.2 proves the basic flow needs richer syntax)
- **C2c visual variant diff** — highlight differences on the schematic / PCB
  canvas (field-level table ships in 0.2.2)
- **C3 — PnS router polish** (length-match groups, hugging, native autorouter)
- **Web dashboard / privacy panel / variants-in-CLI** from MOON-1407 Phase 2

---

## 0.2.4 — Phase D: DSL integration (Zener via forked diodeinc/pcb)

### Why

Current agent → board flow is `agent → IPC tool call → modify board`. Each
edit is an individual IPC roundtrip; agent has no holistic representation
of the design. Switching to `agent → write DSL → compile DSL → board` gives:

- A single source of truth the agent can read/diff in one shot
- Fast compile time (Starlark-based, can re-run on every save)
- Constraint declarations live with the design (not scattered in rules)
- A natural place for project settings (no more "edit this dialog, edit
  that file")
- Round-trip with visual editor: agent can also *read* what a human just
  drew

By 0.2.4 the underlying data model (impedance constraints, variant
scoping, stackup integration, real-time DRC, sch-side diff pairs) lands
in 0.2.2/0.2.3 — Phase D is then a clean encoding problem rather than a
co-design problem.

### Prior art

- **zeo1** was a full Rust rebuild around this concept; too big to land.
  Its `.zeo` language design (in `zeo1/plans/ref/zeo-language-spec.md`)
  is explicitly modeled on Zener.
- **diodeinc/pcb** (Zener language) is the closest external thing, with
  reusable Cargo crates: `pcb-zen` (compiler), `pcb-zen-core` (IR),
  `pcb-sch` (schematic IR), `pcb-kicad` (KiCad output), `pcb-mcp`
  (agent bridge), `pcb-starlark-lsp` (LSP).

### Architecture

```
C++ Zeo (eeschema, pcbnew, agent)
   ◄──IPC──►  kicad-api-rs (existing "zeo-rust"; needs KiCad 10 refresh)
              zeo-zen-bridge (NEW C ABI crate)
                 depends on (forked):
                 - pcb-zen, pcb-zen-core  (compile)
                 - pcb-sch                (schematic IR)
                 - pcb-kicad              (KiCad output)
                 - pcb-starlark-lsp       (LSP for editor)
                 - pcb-mcp                (agent integration path)
                 with Zeo extensions for:
                 - impedance targets       (from 0.2.2 A1)
                 - variant scoping         (from 0.2.2 A6)
                 - sch-side diff pairs     (from 0.2.2 B2)
                 - rigid-flex regions      (from 0.2.3 C4, if landed)
```

The existing `zeo-rust` (kicad-api-rs) stays separate — it's the
live-session IPC. The new `zeo-zen-bridge` is the DSL compile/decompile
engine.

### Phase D scope (0.2.4)

**Foundation (~9 d, 6 tickets):**

- **D1.** Update `zeo-rust` (kicad-api-rs) to current KiCad 10 protobuf
  schema. The bindings have drifted; refresh codegen against
  `api/proto/`. ~1.5 d.
- **D2.** Fork `diodeinc/pcb`; create `zeo-zen-bridge` Cargo crate;
  vendor `pcb-zen`, `pcb-zen-core`, `pcb-sch`, `pcb-kicad`. ~1 d.
- **D3.** Expose C ABI:
  `int zen_compile(const char* zen_path, const char* kicad_sch_out)` →
  invokes `pcb-zen::compile` then `pcb-kicad::emit`. ~3 d.
- **D4.** CMake wiring: build `zeo-zen-bridge` as part of the Zeo build;
  expose to `agent/` and `kicad/` kifaces. ~1 d.
- **D5.** CLI command in Zeo: `Zeo compile path/to/foo.zen` produces
  `.kicad_sch` next to it. ~1 d.
- **D6.** End-to-end smoke test: blinky example (from
  `diodeinc/pcb/examples/blinky.zen`) compiles cleanly, opens in Zeo
  eeschema, looks right. ~1.5 d.

**Zener extensions for Zeo concepts (~10–15 d, 5–7 tickets):**

- **D-ext1.** Impedance target as Zener primitive: `impedance("100ohm",
  tolerance=5%)` constrains a net.
- **D-ext2.** Variant-scoped declarations in Zener (`variant("EU") { ... }`).
- **D-ext3.** Sch-side diff pair declaration in Zener.
- **D-ext4.** Stackup declaration in Zener (project-level).
- **D-ext5.** Round-trip preservation for any sch concept that the
  upstream Zener can't express.
- **D-ext6.** Rigid-flex region declaration (if 0.2.3 C4 lands).

**Full integration (~15–20 d, 6 tickets):**

- **D7.** Schematic → `.zen` decompile path (`pcb-zen` decompile or
  custom emitter from `pcb-sch`). Hard part of round-trip.
- **D8.** Replace agent IPC tool spam with `write_zen` + `compile_zen`
  tools. Agent edits DSL as a coherent design rather than micro-edits.
- **D9.** File watch in running Zeo: `.zen` changes recompile and update
  open schematic. Position-only edits stay in `.kicad_sch`; semantic
  edits round-trip to `.zen`.
- **D10.** Project settings in DSL — `Zeo.toml` / pcb.toml style,
  declares boards, variants, rule files, library deps.
- **D11.** Stdlib vendoring: vendor `diodeinc/pcb/stdlib` (Resistor,
  Capacitor, Diode, etc. as importable Zener modules), extended with
  any Zeo-specific primitives.
- **D12.** LSP integration in Zeo's code editor (if Zeo gets one) or as
  a standalone LSP for external editors.

**0.2.4 total: 17–19 tickets, ~35–45 days.** This is a full release on its own.

### Open questions for 0.2.4

1. **License compatibility.** Zeo is GPL-3.0; diodeinc/pcb's license
   needs verification before fork. If incompatible (e.g. Apache-2.0
   with GPL-incompatible patent clause), the fork strategy still works
   — just relicensed under GPL-3.0 by us as authors of the fork.
2. **Starlark fork churn.** diodeinc maintains its own fork of
   starlark-rust at a pinned rev. Locking to a specific rev is fine for
   our fork; tracking upstream is the maintenance question.
3. **Scope of Zener subset.** Full Zener has modules, generics, registries.
   Investigate which `pcb-zen` features the foundation phase needs to
   expose vs. what waits for the extensions phase.
4. **Replacing the agent's IPC tools.** Once D8 lands, ~half of the
   agent's existing tool registry becomes obsolete. Plan the
   deprecation carefully — keep IPC tools alive for backward compat
   while DSL tools mature.
5. **Co-evolution of upstream pcb-zen.** Our fork will diverge to add
   Zeo concepts. Decide upfront whether to upstream extensions back to
   diodeinc or stay forked.

# Zeo

AI Agent extension for KiCad (open-source EDA software).

## Tech Stack

C++17, wxWidgets, libcurl, nlohmann/json

## Project Structure

```
agent/                  # AI Agent UI and LLM integration
├── agent.cpp           # Entry point (KIFACE factory)
├── agent_frame.cpp     # Main window, chat UI, event handling
├── agent_llm_client.cpp # LLM API client (OpenAI/Anthropic)
├── chat_history.cpp    # JSON persistence
├── core/
│   └── chat_controller.cpp  # Chat state machine
├── tools/
│   ├── tool_schemas.cpp         # Tool definitions (JSON schemas sent to LLM)
│   ├── tool_registry.cpp        # Singleton dispatcher (tool name → handler map)
│   ├── tool_handler.h           # Base interface for all tool handlers
│   ├── handlers/                # Tool handler implementations
│   │   ├── python_tool_handler.cpp  # Loads .py scripts, builds IPC commands (30 tools)
│   │   ├── pcb_autoroute_handler.cpp # Async Freerouting integration
│   │   └── screenshot_handler.cpp   # CLI screenshot capture
│   ├── python/                  # Python scripts (loaded at runtime)
│   │   ├── common/              # Shared utilities (preamble.py, bbox.py)
│   │   ├── schematic/           # sch_*.py (add, update, delete, connect_net, etc.)
│   │   └── pcb/                 # pcb_*.py (add, route, place, export, etc.)
│   └── util/                    # C++ helpers (kicad_cli_util)
├── auth/               # Supabase auth + keychain storage
├── bridge/             # JS↔C++ webview message router
└── view/               # Markdown→HTML, templates, file attachments

api/proto/              # Protobuf definitions for IPC API
├── schematic/          # Schematic commands
└── common/             # Shared types

eeschema/api/           # Schematic editor API handlers
├── api_handler_sch.cpp # IPC command implementations
└── api_handler_sch.h

pcbnew/                 # PCB editor
eeschema/               # Schematic editor
kicad/                  # Project manager
common/                 # Shared libraries
```

## Agent Tools Architecture

Tools follow a layered architecture:
1. **Tool Schema** (`tool_schemas.cpp`) - JSON definitions sent to LLM
2. **Tool Registry** (`tool_registry.cpp`) - Dispatches tool calls to handlers via name → handler map
3. **Tool Handler** (`python_tool_handler.cpp`) - Loads `.py` scripts and builds IPC commands
4. **IPC API** (`api_handler_sch.cpp`) - Handles protobuf commands
5. **Kipy** (`zeo-python/kipy/`) - Python bindings for IPC

For detailed process on adding/updating tools, see `/zeo-python/CLAUDE.md`

## LLM Models

The agent supports multiple Claude models. **Opus (`claude-opus-4-7`) is the preferred model** — all testing and development is done against Opus. Opus 4.6 (`claude-opus-4-6`) and Sonnet 4.6 (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) remain selectable as alternatives.

## Lint / LSP Errors

Ignore clang LSP diagnostic errors. The LSP cannot resolve CMake include paths, so it reports false positives (e.g. `'nlohmann/json.hpp' file not found`). If the build script succeeds, the code is correct.

## Debugging

Logs: `~/Library/Logs/Zeo/agent-<timestamp>.log` (one per session)

For terminal output: `WXTRACE=1 ./Zeo`

#!/bin/bash
# mac_build.sh — unified Zeo macOS build script.
#
# Modes:
#   (default)        Full hard build + install (one-time setup / clean rebuild)
#   --fast           Incremental build (requires a prior hard build)
#   --package        Also create a distributable .dmg after the build
#   --skip-build     Skip build phase entirely (use with --package for DMG-only)
#
# Flags (cross-platform, mirrored in appimage_build.sh / win_build.ps1):
#   --release NAME   Release name (e.g. --release 1.0 → zeo-1.0.dmg)
#   --launch         Launch Zeo.app after build
#   --quit           Kill any running Zeo before the build
#   --target NAME    Build a specific make target (implies --fast)
#   --agent          Shortcut for --target agent --fast
#   --python         Rebuild kipy (Python bindings)
#   --install        Run make install to populate kicad-dest (fast mode)
#   --debug          Launch with WXTRACE=KICAD_AGENT (implies --launch)
#   --lldb           Launch under lldb (implies --launch)
#   --force          Clear cmake cache, full reconfigure
#   --verbose        Show build output in terminal (hard mode)
#   --sign IDENTITY  Code signing identity (--package)
#   --notarize       Apple notarization (--package, requires --sign)
#   --help           Show this help
#
# Internal implementation lives in dev/utils/mac_{hard,fast,dmg}.sh and is
# not intended to be invoked directly.

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
INTERNAL="$SCRIPT_DIR/utils"

# Defaults
MODE=hard          # hard | fast | skip
PACKAGE=false
RELEASE=""
LAUNCH=false
QUIT=false
TARGET=""

176	     *
177	     * Tries to find the parameters that minimizes the error on Z_Diff.
178	     * This function only works with two parameters.
179	     * Calls @ref Analyse several times until the error is acceptable.
180	     * While the error is unacceptable, changes slightly the parameter.
181	     *
182	     * This function does not change Z0 / Angl_L

content.text:
That's the expression parser — KiCad's rule expressions need an item-context prefix (`A.`) for all registered functions. Same as `A.existsOnLayer('F.Cu')`.

Change line 3 to:

```
(condition "A.variantIs('Production')")
```

The full rule:
```
(rule "var-only"
  (condition "A.variantIs('Production')")
  (constraint impedance_target (min 85) (max 95)))
```

The `A.` binds the call to "the item being checked" — my implementation just reads `item->GetBoard()->GetCurrentVariant()` from there, so any track on the board will resolve correctly.

content.text:
Test plan for the 8 still-unverified surfaces. Use one board with at least one named variant (e.g. `Production`) and a small impedance test rule already in place from earlier sessions.

**1. C2d — variant in window title** (fastest sanity check)
- Switch variant in PCB toolbar → window title should show `[Variant: Production]`. Switch back to default → suffix disappears.
- Same in schematic editor.
- *Fail mode*: title doesn't update → `UpdateTitle()` / `updateTitle()` wasn't fired.

**2. C2a — properties dialog banner**
- With `Production` active, double-click a symbol in schematic → bold orange banner at top says `Editing variant 'Production' — changes to fields below create variant-specific overrides.`
- Switch to base variant, open same dialog → no banner.
- Same flow in PCB editor for footprint properties.
- *Fail mode*: no banner shown despite active variant → `Schematic().GetCurrentVariant()` returned empty unexpectedly.

**3. A4 + B1a + B1b — router status overlay** (test together)
- Add custom rule: `(rule "narrow" (constraint track_width (min 0.5mm) (max 1mm)))`
- Save, start routing (`X`) with track width set to 0.2mm
- Push into an obstacle so PNS triggers "Track violates DRC"
- Status overlay should now read:
  ```
  Track violates DRC.
  (narrow: width 0.2mm < 0.5mm)
      Z₀ = N Ω
  ```
- For B1b VIA_DIAMETER: add `(constraint via_diameter (min 0.8mm))` and place a 0.4mm via.
- For B1b DISALLOW: add `(rule "no-cu-top" (condition "A.Layer == 'F.Cu'") (constraint disallow track))` and try to route on F.Cu.
- *Fail mode*: only generic "Track violates DRC" shows → `buildDrcViolationDetail()` returned empty (check the rule actually matches your selection's net/layer).

**4. B2 — schematic context menu diff-pair**
- In schematic, right-click on a labeled wire (e.g. `USB_DP`) → menu shows `Mark as Diff Pair...`
- Click it → dialog "Pair net 'USB_DP' with:" with sorted list of other nets
- Pick `USB_DN` → message bar shows `Diff pair declared: USB_DP ↔ USB_DN`
- Open the project file in a text editor — `multi_board.cross_board_diff_pairs` should now contain the pair.
- *Fail mode*: menu entry doesn't appear → selection wasn't a label/wire (`markAsDiffPairCondition` filter), or the net has no name.

**5. C2b — BOM variant dropdown**
- Tools → Generate Bill of Materials
- Variant dropdown above buttons; default `(All / base)`, then your variant names
- Pick `Production`, click Generate → BOM xml gets variant-filtered values
- Check schematic toolbar variant indicator before/after — should be unchanged (the dialog restores).
- *Fail mode*: BOM doesn't reflect variant → `WriteNetListFile` doesn't read `Schematic().GetCurrentVariant()`. Compare BOM contents between Base and Production runs.

**6. C2c — variant diff dialog**
- Tools → Variants → Compare Variants...
- Two pickers at top, list view below with columns: Reference / Field / Variant A / Variant B
- Defaults to Base ↔ first variant; shows rows for every field that differs
- Change picker → list rebuilds
- Pick same variant on both sides → "Pick two different variants…" message
- *Fail mode*: dialog empty when you know overrides exist → `GetFieldText(fieldName, &sheet, variant)` isn't returning overrides; check field name canonicalization.

**Edge cases worth covering**
- A4 + B1a/B1b with no impedance/track-width rules at all → overlay should still show base message, no crashes (empty suffix expected).
- C2c with zero variants → both pickers only have `(Base)`, comparison is trivially empty.
- B2 on an unnamed wire (no label nearby) → info bar error: `"Selected item is not on a named net."`

If any of these fail, send the symptom + screenshot and I'll diagnose.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

{"id":"MOON-1417","title":"A1: Add IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT to DRC rule engine","description":"## Summary

Add a new constraint type `IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT` to the DRC rule engine, enabling rule authors to declare per-net or per-class impedance targets that downstream tickets will enforce.

## Context

KiCad's DRC engine has 36 constraint types (`pcbnew/drc/drc_rule.h:47–86`) — clearance, length, diff-pair gap, etc. — but none for impedance. The trunk realization for Zeo 0.2.2 is that constraints + stackup + signal integrity are one tightly coupled trio. The stackup already carries Dk/Df, and `common/transline_calculations/` already has microstrip/stripline calculators. What's missing is the constraint *language* — a way to say "this net should be 50 Ω" in rules.

This ticket adds only the constraint type, parser, and error code. Evaluation lives in A2 (test provider). UI lives in A3/A4/A5.

## Implementation

* `pcbnew/drc/drc_rule.h:85–86` — add `IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT` enum value after `MAX_UNCOUPLED_CONSTRAINT` (SI-family grouping)
* `common/drc_rules.keywords` (\~line 28, alphabetical) — add `impedance_target`
* `pcbnew/drc/drc_rule_parser.cpp:499–558` — add parse case mirroring `LENGTH_CONSTRAINT`:

  ```cpp
  case T_impedance_target: c.m_Type = IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT; break;
  ```

  Uses the existing `MINOPTMAX<int>` triple. Internal units: milli-ohms. Rule file accepts integer ohms.
* `include/drc_item.h` — add `DRCE_IMPEDANCE_MISMATCH` error code for downstream test provider use.
* Do NOT add to the `unitless` check (impedance has units) or `allowsTimeDomain` check (impedance is spatial).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rule like `(rule "high-speed" (constraint impedance_target (min 48) (opt 50) (max 52)))` parses without error
- [ ] Unit test in `qa/tests/pcbnew/` covering parse success + invalid-syntax rejection
- [ ] Existing DRC rules continue to parse without regression

## Effort & dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1423","title":"A2: DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_IMPEDANCE — enforce impedance targets from stackup","description":"## Summary

Implement the test provider that consumes `IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT` (from A1), reads the stackup's Dk/Df, calls the existing transline calculator, and emits a DRC violation when a track's computed Z₀ falls outside the rule's MIN/MAX.

## Context

The transline calculators (`common/transline_calculations/microstrip.h`, `stripline.h`, etc.) already compute Z₀ from geometry + dielectric. They're used today by the tuning profile dialog only. This ticket wires them into DRC so impedance becomes a queryable, enforceable constraint — the core load-bearing piece of Phase A.

## Implementation

* **New files:** `pcbnew/drc/drc_test_provider_impedance.{h,cpp}`
* Class `DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_IMPEDANCE` derives from `DRC_TEST_PROVIDER` (pattern: `drc_test_provider_matched_length.cpp:43–72`)
* `Run()` → `runInternal()` → iterate `PCB_TRACK_T`, `PCB_ARC_T`, `PCB_VIA_T` via `forEachGeometryItem()` (pattern: `drc_test_provider_matched_length.cpp:374–400`)
* For each track:
  * Query rule: `m_drcEngine->EvalRules(IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT, track, nullptr, track->GetLayer())`
  * If constraint applies, look up adjacent dielectric via `BOARD_STACKUP::GetLayerDistance()` and `BOARD_STACKUP_ITEM::DIELECTRIC_PRMS` (Dk, Df, thickness)
  * Pick `MICROSTRIP` (outer layer) or `STRIPLINE` (inner layer)
  * Set params: `H` (substrate height), `T` (copper thickness), `PHYS_WIDTH`, `EPSILONR` (Dk), `TAND` (Df)
  * Call `Analyse()`; read `Z0` from `GetParameter(TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS::Z0)`
  * Compare against constraint MIN/MAX; emit `DRC_ITEM::Create(DRCE_IMPEDANCE_MISMATCH)` if out of range
* Auto-register with `DRC_REGISTER_TEST_PROVIDER<DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_IMPEDANCE>` at file scope

## Caching

Mirror `m_netclassClearances` pattern from `drc_engine.h:374–398`:

* New cache: `std::unordered_map<DRC_IMPEDANCE_CACHE_KEY, int> m_impedanceCache` keyed by `{netcode, layer, width}`
* Populate in test provider; invalidate on board changes via existing invalidation hooks
* Factor a shared helper (used by A3/A4/A5) so router and dialog UI compute Z₀ the same way

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rule from A1 (`impedance_target`) generates DRC violations on tracks outside the target range
- [ ] Microstrip Z₀ calculation matches the existing tuning profile dialog's calculation for the same inputs
- [ ] Stripline path works for inner-layer tracks
- [ ] Cache prevents recomputation across DRC runs unless stackup or geometry changes

{"id":"MOON-1423","title":"A2: DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_IMPEDANCE — enforce impedance targets from stackup","description":"## Summary

Implement the test provider that consumes `IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT` (from A1), reads the stackup's Dk/Df, calls the existing transline calculator, and emits a DRC violation when a track's computed Z₀ falls outside the rule's MIN/MAX.

## Context

The transline calculators (`common/transline_calculations/microstrip.h`, `stripline.h`, etc.) already compute Z₀ from geometry + dielectric. They're used today by the tuning profile dialog only. This ticket wires them into DRC so impedance becomes a queryable, enforceable constraint — the core load-bearing piece of Phase A.

## Implementation

* **New files:** `pcbnew/drc/drc_test_provider_impedance.{h,cpp}`
* Class `DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_IMPEDANCE` derives from `DRC_TEST_PROVIDER` (pattern: `drc_test_provider_matched_length.cpp:43–72`)
* `Run()` → `runInternal()` → iterate `PCB_TRACK_T`, `PCB_ARC_T`, `PCB_VIA_T` via `forEachGeometryItem()` (pattern: `drc_test_provider_matched_length.cpp:374–400`)
* For each track:
  * Query rule: `m_drcEngine->EvalRules(IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT, track, nullptr, track->GetLayer())`
  * If constraint applies, look up adjacent dielectric via `BOARD_STACKUP::GetLayerDistance()` and `BOARD_STACKUP_ITEM::DIELECTRIC_PRMS` (Dk, Df, thickness)
  * Pick `MICROSTRIP` (outer layer) or `STRIPLINE` (inner layer)
  * Set params: `H` (substrate height), `T` (copper thickness), `PHYS_WIDTH`, `EPSILONR` (Dk), `TAND` (Df)
  * Call `Analyse()`; read `Z0` from `GetParameter(TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS::Z0)`
  * Compare against constraint MIN/MAX; emit `DRC_ITEM::Create(DRCE_IMPEDANCE_MISMATCH)` if out of range
* Auto-register with `DRC_REGISTER_TEST_PROVIDER<DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_IMPEDANCE>` at file scope

## Caching

Mirror `m_netclassClearances` pattern from `drc_engine.h:374–398`:

* New cache: `std::unordered_map<DRC_IMPEDANCE_CACHE_KEY, int> m_impedanceCache` keyed by `{netcode, layer, width}`
* Populate in test provider; invalidate on board changes via existing invalidation hooks
* Factor a shared helper (used by A3/A4/A5) so router and dialog UI compute Z₀ the same way

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rule from A1 (`impedance_target`) generates DRC violations on tracks outside the target range
- [ ] Microstrip Z₀ calculation matches the existing tuning profile dialog's calculation for the same inputs
- [ ] Stripline path works for inner-layer tracks
- [ ] Cache prevents recomputation across DRC runs unless stackup or geometry changes

{"id":"MOON-1428","title":"A3: Computed impedance in track properties dialog","description":"## Summary

Display computed Z₀ in the Track & Via Properties dialog so the user sees impedance when editing track width / layer / net assignment.

## Context

A2 (<issue id="afa65e5e-6e43-4392-a62e-c8434dcb3336">MOON-1423</issue>) wires impedance into DRC. This ticket surfaces the same computation in the most natural place for a user to see it: the dialog where they edit a track's width.

## Implementation

* `pcbnew/dialogs/dialog_track_via_size.{h,cpp}` (and `.fbp` if applicable)
* Add read-only `wxTextCtrl m_computedImpedance` to the dialog
* Populate on `OnInit()` and update on `OnWidthChange()`, `OnLayerChange()`:
  * Call into the shared Z₀ helper factored in A2 (so router, dialog, net inspector all agree)
  * Format: `"%.2f Ω"`; show "—" if stackup info missing
* Field is read-only — informational, not editable

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dialog opens on a track; impedance field populates if stackup has Dk/Df
- [ ] Changing width triggers recompute
- [ ] Changing layer triggers recompute (microstrip ↔ stripline switch)
- [ ] No regression on dialog accept/cancel behavior
- [ ] If stackup info missing, field shows "—" without crashing

## Effort & dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1430","title":"A5: Impedance column in Net Inspector","description":"## Summary

Add an average-impedance column to the Net Inspector panel for at-a-glance review of nets that should be impedance-controlled.

## Context

The Net Inspector at `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel.{h,cpp}` is where users see per-net statistics (length, via count, etc.). Adding Z₀ makes impedance a first-class observable alongside length.

## Implementation

* `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel.h:308–321` — insert `COLUMN_AVG_IMPEDANCE` before `COLUMN_LAST_STATIC_COL`
* `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel_data_model.h`:
  * Add `double m_avg_impedance` to `LIST_ITEM`
  * Add `AvgImpedanceChanged() / SetAvgImpedance()` methods following existing pattern
  * Add `GetValue()` case for `COLUMN_AVG_IMPEDANCE`
* `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel.cpp::buildNetsList()`:
  * For each net, iterate its tracks; compute Z₀ per track via the shared helper from A2; average across the net
  * Set `m_avg_impedance` on the list item

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New "Avg Z₀" column visible in Net Inspector
- [ ] Sortable
- [ ] Updates on board changes that affect track geometry
- [ ] Empty for nets without tracks on copper layers

## Effort & dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1418","title":"A6: variantIs() expression function for variant-scoped DRC rules","description":"## Summary

Add `variantIs(name)` to the DRC rule expression evaluator so rules can be conditionally scoped to the active variant.

## Context

KiCad has a working variant system (`BOARD::GetCurrentVariant()` at `board.h:427`, `m_currentVariant` at `board.h:1681`). The DRC rules engine evaluates condition expressions via `pcbexpr_evaluator.cpp` but has no way to reference the active variant. This ticket adds a single function so rule authors can write:

```
(rule "EU stricter clearance"
  (condition "variantIs('EU')")
  (constraint clearance (min 0.3mm)))
```

## Implementation

* `pcbnew/pcbexpr_evaluator.cpp` — add `variantIs(name)` returning `1.0` if `m_board->GetCurrentVariant() == name`, else `0.0`
* `pcbnew/pcbexpr_functions.cpp` — register `variantIs` in the function registry (find an analogous single-arg function registration and mirror)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rule with `(condition "variantIs('foo')")` only fires when active variant is "foo"
- [ ] Case-insensitive match (per existing variant lookup convention)
- [ ] Unit test in `qa/tests/pcbnew/`

## Effort & dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1420","title":"C2a: Explicit variant override indicator in properties dialogs","description":"## Summary

When a user edits a field in symbol or footprint properties with an active variant, show an explicit visual indicator that the edit creates a variant-specific override.

## Context

Per audit, variant overrides currently happen **implicitly** in the properties dialogs. The user has no way to know that editing the "Value" field with variant "EU" active creates a per-variant override rather than changing the base value. This is the single biggest variants UX gap — users regularly make accidental overrides or edit a "base" value that does nothing because they're in variant-specific mode.

## Implementation

Files:

* `eeschema/dialogs/dialog_symbol_properties.cpp:408–796`
* `pcbnew/dialogs/dialog_footprint_properties.cpp:255–672`

Changes:

* When dialog opens with a non-empty active variant:
  * Show a clearly-visible banner at the top: **"Editing variant: \[variant_name\] — changes to fields create per-variant overrides on this instance"**
* Per-field indicator:
  * If a field has a variant-specific override: badge / colored background next to the field (mirror pattern from `eeschema/fields_data_model.cpp:437–542` which highlights overridden cells yellow in the fields table)
  * Tooltip: "Overridden in variant \[name\]. Base value: \[base\]"
* Add a "Revert to base" context menu / button per overridden field

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dialog opened with an active variant shows the banner
- [ ] Editing any field with variant active creates an explicit override (existing behavior, now visible)
- [ ] Fields already overridden show the badge
- [ ] "Revert to base" removes the override
- [ ] Dialog with no active variant looks identical to before

## Effort & dependencies

\~1.5 days. Add a variant selector to the BOM export dialog so users can generate per-variant BOMs without going through the CLI.

## Context

Per audit, BOM filtering by variant works at the data layer (`BOM_PRESET::excludeDNP`) and via `kicad-cli` (`test_job_export_pcb_variants.cpp`). The dialog at `eeschema/dialogs/dialog_bom.cpp` has no variant UI — users editing in the GUI can't pick a variant. Existing variant-aware export dialogs to mirror:

* `pcbnew/dialogs/dialog_export_step.cpp:250–638` (`m_choiceVariant` dropdown)

## Implementation

* `eeschema/dialogs/dialog_bom.cpp` (and its `.fbp` if applicable) — add `m_choiceVariant` dropdown

* Include "All variants" / "Default" option for unchanged behavior

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting a variant filters DNP'd components per the variant
- [ ] Variant-specific field overrides reflected in BOM output
- [ ] "All variants" option preserves current default behavior
- [ ] Output matches CLI `kicad-cli sch export bom --variant <name>` for the same variant

{"id":"MOON-1422","title":"C2c: Field-level variant-diff viewer","description":"## Summary

New dialog to pick two variants and see a side-by-side table of fields that differ between them.

## Context

Per audit, there is no way to see "what changed between variant A and variant B." Field-level diff is straightforward; visual canvas diff (highlighting symbols/footprints on the schematic / PCB canvas itself) is bigger and explicitly deferred to **0.2.3**.

## Implementation

* New dialog: `eeschema/dialogs/dialog_variant_diff.{cpp,h,fbp}` (start with a basic `wxGrid`, no need for the form builder if simpler)
* Inputs: two variant dropdowns
* Table columns: **Instance | Field | Variant A value | Variant B value**
* Iterate `VARIANT::GetFieldOverrides()` for both variants; show rows where values differ or one variant has an override the other lacks
* Filters:
  * "Show only differences" (default ON)
  * "Group by component" (default ON)
* Accessible from **Tools → Variants → Compare…**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dialog opens from Tools > Variants > Compare…
- [ ] Selecting two variants shows their field-level differences
- [ ] "All fields" mode shows fields even when equal between variants
- [ ] Identical-variant comparison shows empty diff
- [ ] No regression on existing variant operations

## Effort & dependencies

content.subject: A1: Add IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT enum + parser
content.description: MOON-1417. Add enum value to drc_rule.h, keyword to drc_rules.keywords, parser case in drc_rule_parser.cpp, DRCE_IMPEDANCE_MISMATCH in drc_item.h. Pattern from LENGTH_CONSTRAINT. Uses MINOPTMAX<int> (milli-ohms).

content.subject: A6: Add variantIs() DRC expression function
content.description: MOON-1418. Add variantIs(name) to pcbexpr_evaluator.cpp + register in pcbexpr_functions.cpp. Reads BOARD::GetCurrentVariant(). Parallelizable with A1.

content.subject: A2: DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_IMPEDANCE
content.description: MOON-1423. New file pcbnew/drc/drc_test_provider_impedance.cpp/.h. Iterates tracks via forEachGeometryItem; reads stackup Dk/Df via BOARD_STACKUP; calls MICROSTRIP/STRIPLINE Analyse(); emits DRC_ITEM on violation. Cache mirrors m_netclassClearances.

content.subject: A3: Computed impedance in track properties dialog
content.description: MOON-1428. Add read-only wxTextCtrl for computed Z₀ in dialog_track_via_size.h/.cpp; populate on width/layer/net change.

content.subject: A4: Z₀ display in PNS router status bar
content.description: MOON-1429. Append Z₀ = X.X Ω to router status at router_tool.cpp:2128, 2690 via statusItem->AppendMessage().

content.subject: A5: Impedance column in Net Inspector
content.description: MOON-1430. Add COLUMN_AVG_IMPEDANCE before COLUMN_LAST_STATIC_COL in pcb_net_inspector_panel.h; add m_avg_impedance to data model; compute per-net average Z₀ in buildNetsList().

content.subject: B1a: Real-time DRC spike (TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT)
content.description: MOON-1424. SPIKE — needs runtime latency measurement (target <2ms/segment) before committing to full rollout. Remaining: populate detail string in PNS_PCBNEW_RULE_RESOLVER::QueryConstraint for CT_WIDTH; wire to router_tool.cpp violation display; measure actual cost in interactive routing. content.subject: B1b: Real-time DRC rollout (4 more constraints)
content.description: MOON-1431. Extended buildDrcViolationDetail with VIA_DIAMETER + DISALLOW constraints. TRACK_ANGLE (needs segment geometry) and VIA_COUNT (needs net-wide traversal) deferred — those require evaluation inside PNS per-segment loop, not at status display time.

content.description: MOON-1420. Added a prominent orange/bold banner at top of symbol+footprint properties dialogs when editing under an active variant. ## Context

The PNS router currently shows "Track violates DRC" (generic) at `router_tool.cpp:2128, 2690`. Adding a live Z₀ readout gives the user immediate feedback on whether they're hitting an impedance target — equivalent to what Altium surfaces during interactive routing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Z₀ shows in router status while routing
- [ ] Updates as the user changes width / layer mid-route
- [ ] No measurable perf regression on the router event loop (interactive path)
- [ ] Visible only when stackup info available — falls back gracefully otherwise

{"id":"MOON-1424","title":"B1a: Real-time DRC spike — TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT in interactive routing","description":"## Summary

Prototype real-time DRC during interactive routing by extending PNS to evaluate `TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT` per segment. Measure latency before committing to full rollout (B1b).

## Context

Per audit, PNS already calls `DRC_ENGINE::EvalRules()` per segment for clearance/width/gap geometry (`pcbnew/router/pns_kicad_iface.cpp:434–680`). The gap to Altium is full rule-set evaluation with rule-name violation details. The audit identified 5 high-leverage constraints feasible per-segment at total \~1.2 ms cost. This spike validates that budget with the simplest one (track width).

## Implementation

* `pcbnew/router/pns_node.h:72–81` — extend `PNS::CONSTRAINT` struct:

  ```cpp
  wxString m_ViolationDetail;
  ```
* `pcbnew/router/pns_kicad_iface.cpp:434–684` — extend `PNS_PCBNEW_RULE_RESOLVER::QueryConstraint()` to handle `TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT`:
  * Build a `PCB_TRACK` proxy from the in-flight `PNS::LINE`
  * Call `EvalRules(TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT, ...)`
  * Populate `m_ViolationDetail` with formatted "min W; actual W"
* `pcbnew/router/router_tool.cpp:2120–2135` — replace generic "Track violates DRC" with formatted detail list:

  ```
  Track violates DRC:
    - Track width (min 0.25mm; actual 0.20mm)
  ```
* `pcbnew/router/router_status_view_item.{h,cpp}::ViewDraw()` — render multi-line detail

## Performance instrumentation

* Add `std::chrono` timer around `QueryConstraint()`; log per-call latency at debug level
* Target: <2 ms/segment for the single TRACK_WIDTH check
* If >3 ms, investigate batch via `DRC_CLEARANCE_BATCH` pattern (`drc_engine.h:111–118`) before opening B1b

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Drawing a track narrower than rule-defined minimum shows specific "track width" violation in status (not the generic message)
- [ ] Interactive routing latency unchanged subjectively at 60 FPS
- [ ] Measured per-segment cost recorded as a comment on this ticket before closing
- [ ] No regression on the existing clearance/width/gap geometric checks

## Effort & dependencies

\~2 days. **Blocked by:** A1 (<issue id="d24cfb68-65f2-4a21-983f-3cc0173c34b3">MOON-1417</issue>) for the constraint enum extension. **Blocks:** B1b.","projectMilestone":{"id":"6d6200e6-c322-4407-b60d-06cf6b252bea","name":"0.3.0"},"priority":{"value":2,"name":"High"},"url":"https://linear.app/distillmoonshine/issue/MOON-1424/b1a-real-time-drc-spike-track-width-constraint-in-interactive-routing","gitBranchName":"ganesh/moon-1424-b1a-real-time-drc-spike-track_width_constraint-in","createdAt":"2026-05-19T02:17:44.842Z","updatedAt":"2026-05-26T17:56:32.625Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-05-26T17:56:32.603Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"In Review","statusType":"started","labels":["Feature"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Ganesh Pimpale","createdById":"4ea6e562-99b6-4d8b-ad51-653d882bcd6d","project":"Zeo 0.3.0","projectId":"4d2a32db-e877-47d4-80e3-5094d1a90cd2","team":"Moonshine","teamId":"84a83d69-1dbb-491d-9b85-7613ecfe1619"}

{"id":"MOON-1431","title":"B1b: Real-time DRC rollout — VIA_DIAMETER, TRACK_ANGLE, DISALLOW, VIA_COUNT","description":"## Summary

Extend the per-segment rule evaluation from B1a (<issue id="4030d4b4-db10-4cf5-ba4b-a52d47fa65a7">MOON-1424</issue>) to the remaining 4 high-leverage constraints, validating total latency budget (\~1.2 ms/segment) is met.

## Context

Per audit Part 5, these 5 constraints are highest-value during interactive routing:

1. TRACK_WIDTH_CONSTRAINT (done in B1a)
2. VIA_DIAMETER_CONSTRAINT (\~0.05 ms)
3. TRACK_ANGLE_CONSTRAINT (\~0.2 ms)
4. DISALLOW_CONSTRAINT (\~0.5 ms, RTree-cached)
5. VIA_COUNT_CONSTRAINT (\~0.3 ms)

LENGTH/SKEW remain too expensive per segment (\~50–100 ms due to cross-board graph walks) and stay batch-only.

## Implementation

For each constraint, extend `PNS_PCBNEW_RULE_RESOLVER::QueryConstraint()` at `pcbnew/router/pns_kicad_iface.cpp:434–684` following the B1a pattern:

* **VIA_DIAMETER:** When inserting a via during routing, evaluate against rule. Single property check \~0.05 ms.
* **TRACK_ANGLE:** Use `connectivity->GetConnectedTracks()` to find prior segment; compute angle; evaluate. Local neighbor query \~0.2 ms.
* **DISALLOW:** Leverage `drc_test_provider_disallow.cpp:114–185` RTree cache pattern. Add incremental RTree maintenance: when the router moves, ensure the cache reflects the current zone set. \~0.5 ms with cache.
* **VIA_COUNT:** Count vias on current net via active routing path only (not full board). Use connectivity queries scoped to the in-flight route. \~0.3 ms typical.

Each constraint emits a specific `m_ViolationDetail` string via the struct extension from B1a.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the 4 constraints emits specific violation detail during routing (e.g., "Via diameter (min 0.4mm; actual 0.3mm)")
- [ ] Total per-segment cost <2 ms (measured across all 5 constraints including B1a's TRACK_WIDTH)
- [ ] Interactive routing still runs at 60+ FPS on a 1000-track board
- [ ] DISALLOW correctly re-queries when keepout zones change mid-session
- [ ] Measurements recorded as a comment on this ticket before closing

## Effort & dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1425","title":"B2: Schematic-side diff-pair declaration ergonomics","description":"## Summary

Make the existing diff-pair declaration mechanism (`PROJECT_FILE::GetCrossBoardDiffPairs()` / `NETCLASS` diff-pair properties) reachable directly from the schematic context menu, so users don't need to dig into board / project settings to declare a USB / DDR / LVDS pair.

## Context

Per audit, KiCad already supports diff-pair declarations at two levels:

* Project-level: `PROJECT_FILE::GetCrossBoardDiffPairs()` / `AddCrossBoardDiffPair()`
* Netclass: `NETCLASS::GetDiffPairWidth() / GetDiffPairGap()`

The gap is **ergonomics, not mechanism**. A user designing a USB interface should be able to right-click two net labels on the schematic and say "declare as diff pair," persisting via the existing mechanism. **No new file format, no new s-expr** — decision locked 2026-05-15.

## Implementation

* Find the schematic context-menu hook for net labels (`SCH_LABEL`, `SCH_HIERLABEL`); likely in an event-handling region of eeschema
* Add menu item: **"Declare as Differential Pair…"**
* Action: prompt for partner net (or accept current selection if two net labels are selected); call `PROJECT_FILE::AddCrossBoardDiffPair()` and/or assign both nets to a netclass with diff-pair properties
* Optional small dialog for confirming partner net + naming convention (`_P` / `_N`, `+` / `-`)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Right-click on a net label shows "Declare as Differential Pair"
- [ ] Selecting two labels and using the action pairs them
- [ ] Pair persists in project file; visible in PCB rules editor and PCB router diff-pair mode
- [ ] Undo works
- [ ] No new s-expr keywords introduced; existing project-level mechanism reused

## Effort & dependencies

\~1.5 days. **Blocked by:** A1 (<issue id="d24cfb68-65f2-4a21-983f-3cc0173c34b3">MOON-1417</issue>) — only weakly; needs the constraint rule scoping context to live alongside diff-pair rule.","projectMilestone":{"id":"6d6200e6-c322-4407-b60d-06cf6b252bea","name":"0.3.0"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/distillmoonshine/issue/MOON-1425/b2-schematic-side-diff-pair-declaration-ergonomics","gitBranchName":"ganesh/moon-1425-b2-schematic-side-diff-pair-declaration-ergonomics","createdAt":"2026-05-19T02:17:48.546Z","updatedAt":"2026-05-26T17:56:38.826Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-05-26T17:56:38.807Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"In Review","statusType":"started","labels":["Feature"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Ganesh Pimpale","createdById":"4ea6e562-99b6-4d8b-ad51-653d882bcd6d","project":"Zeo 0.3.0","projectId":"4d2a32db-e877-47d4-80e3-5094d1a90cd2","team":"Moonshine","teamId":"84a83d69-1dbb-491d-9b85-7613ecfe1619"}
