content.text:
Researched it — and Altium's structure cleanly answers all three questions, including the per-signal one.

## How Altium actually does it

- **It's all inside the Layer Stack Manager**, not a separate Signal Integrity panel. The Layer Stack Manager has a **dedicated "Impedance" tab** alongside the "Stackup" tab. (The separate *Signal Integrity* analysis tool under Tools is a different, IBIS-model loss/reflection simulator — not where impedance setup lives.)
- **Frequency is a single stackup-wide setting** — default **1 GHz**, Wideband Debye. It is **not per-profile and not per-net.** Altium offers **no per-signal frequency at all.**
- **Per-net control in Altium = the impedance *profile* (target Z + tolerance), assigned via design rules** ("Use Impedance Profile" in the Width routing rule, scoped to a net/net-class). The *target* is per-net; the *frequency* is global.
- Roughness + etch live **per impedance-profile** in the Impedance tab; Dk/Df come from the material library per dielectric.

## What that means for our three questions

**1) Stackup panel vs. new SI panel** → Altium's answer is a *dedicated impedance area grouped with the stackup*, not a top-level SI panel and not crammed into the material grid. The KiCad-idiomatic equivalent: **a new sub-page under the "Board Stackup" group** in Board Setup, called **"Impedance"** — holding the analysis frequency + conductor resistivity + roughness now, with room for impedance *profiles* later. This satisfies your "may warrant a new panel" instinct *and* matches Altium (a separate tab, but under the stack manager — not under Design Rules).

**2) Per-signal frequency — here's the data you asked for.** Your chosen reference tool **does not do per-signal frequency.** Altium uses one global frequency (1 GHz) for the whole board. The reason it still feels like "control" is that the per-net knob is the **impedance target**, not frequency — and *we already have that* (the `impedance_target` DRC constraint from A1/A2, assignable per net/class, plus per-netclass tuning profiles).

So "per-signal control" splits into two things:
- **Per-signal impedance target** (USB = 90 Ω, DDR = 40 Ω) — common, valuable, **already built.**
- **Per-signal frequency** (the analysis frequency itself) — **rare**; no mainstream controlled-impedance flow exposes it. It barely moves Z₀ (we established this), and the place it *does* matter — loss/insertion-loss — is a dedicated SI-simulator feature (HyperLynx/Sigrity do per-net frequency *sweeps*, not a stored per-net value).

My honest recommendation: **go global, like Altium.** You keep per-net control where it belongs (the impedance target, already done), avoid a knob the reference tool deliberately omits, and keep the model simple. If you later want true per-net loss modeling, that's a separate SI-analysis feature where per-net frequency naturally lives.

**3) Ergonomics** — confirmed, value + unit (GHz / µm / µΩ·cm).

## Proposed plan

New **"Board Stackup → Impedance"** sub-page in Board Setup with: reference frequency (GHz), Dk-measurement frequency (GHz), conductor resistivity (µΩ·cm), copper roughness (µm) — bound to the Phase-1a `m_SI_*` fields. **Global frequency.** Per-net stays on the impedance target we already have.

Does that land for you — global frequency + a dedicated Impedance sub-page under Board Stackup? Or do you still want me to wire per-signal frequency (via the tuning profile) despite Altium not doing it?

Sources: [Altium — configuring layer stack for controlled impedance](https://www.altium.com/documentation/altium-designer/configuring-layer-stack-controlled-impedance-routing), [Altium impedance profiles + design rules](https://resources.altium.com/p/impedance-controlled-routing-for-boards-made-in-altium-designer), [Altium stackup impedance calculator](https://resources.altium.com/p/pcb-stackup-impedance-calculator).

The Djordjevic-Sarkar (DS) Debye model is one of the most commonly used extrapolation techniques used to predict broadband electrical performance of dielectric materials from a single-point measurement. Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Djordjevic-Sarkar causal dielectric model:

## Overview

The Djordjevic-Sarkar model was proposed in the paper "Wideband Frequency-Domain Characterization of FR-4 and Time-Domain Causality" published in IEEE Trans. on Electromagnetic Compatibility in November 2001, for modeling the frequency dependence of complex relative permittivity in FR-4 dielectric materials.

## Key Characteristics

This model is an analytic function and hence causal in the time domain. It is very simple and only five parameters define it. It uses an infinite distribution of poles to model the frequency response, and in particular the nearly constant loss tangent of these materials.

## Frequency Bounds

The loss tangent predicted by the model has two transition frequencies, the first around 10³ Hz and the second around 10¹¹ Hz, with the lower transition frequency evident in the experimental data for FR-4 and the upper transition frequency best thought of as a fitting parameter.

## Implementation

This model was developed for low-loss dielectric materials (particularly FR-4) commonly used in printed circuit boards and packages, and HFSS allows you to enter the relative permittivity and loss tangent at a single measurement frequency. The model satisfies the Kramers-Kronig conditions for causality, and so is preferred for applications such as TDR or Full-Wave SPICE where time-domain results are needed.

content.content:
# Djordjevic-Sarkar Model Equations

## Complex Relative Permittivity

The model is defined by equation (9) in the article:

$$\varepsilon_r(\omega) = \varepsilon_\infty + \frac{\Delta\varepsilon}{1 + j\omega/\omega_A} - j\frac{\sigma_{DC}}{\omega\varepsilon_0}$$

where:
- $\varepsilon_\infty$ = permittivity at very high frequency
- $\Delta\varepsilon = \varepsilon_s - \varepsilon_\infty$ = magnitude of dispersion
- $\sigma_{DC}$ = conductivity at DC (low frequency)
- $\omega_A$ = lower angular frequency cutoff
- $\omega_B$ = upper angular frequency cutoff
- The model uses "an infinite distribution of poles"

## Parameter Extraction from Single Measurement

Given a measurement at frequency $f_1$ with relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r$ and loss tangent $\tan\delta$:

The permittivity is decomposed into real and imaginary parts (equations 12-13). If DC conductivity $\sigma_{DC}$ is known, parameters are extracted via equation (15). 

When DC conductivity is unknown, the article states: "a heuristic approximation is De = 10 ε∞ tan δ1" (where De represents $\Delta\varepsilon$).

The document does not explicitly provide the complete closed-form expressions for computing $\varepsilon_\infty$, $\omega_A$, or $\omega_B$ from a single measurement.

content.text:
All three phases are in and building. Here's where the impedance data model stands — the full Altium-parity flow is now live:

## What's done

**Phase 1a** — frequency + material properties are real, controllable inputs (board-level), replacing the old hardcoded `1 GHz / copper / 0-roughness`. Plus the earlier correctness fixes (real loss tangent, dielectric sublayer weighting).

**Phase 2** — **Board Setup → Board Stackup → Impedance** page (mirrors Altium's Impedance tab) to edit reference frequency, Dk-measurement frequency, conductor resistivity, copper roughness.

**Phase 1b** — **Djordjevic-Sarkar causal Dk(f) dispersion**. The bulk Dk/Df now track frequency via the wideband-Debye model (1 kHz–1 THz band), solved to reproduce your datasheet Dk/Df exactly at the measurement frequency. This is what makes the reference-frequency knob *meaningfully* move Z₀ — especially on **inner/stripline layers**, where material Dk(f) is the only frequency dependence.

## Full test pass

1. **Board Setup → Board Stackup → Impedance** → set **Dk specified at frequency = 1 GHz** (your datasheet point), **Reference frequency = 1 GHz** → OK. Note a track's Z₀ (track props or Net Inspector). This is your baseline — should match the pre-change number.
2. Change **Reference frequency → 10 GHz** → OK, reopen. Dk drops (dispersion) → **Z₀ rises a few %**. An inner-layer (stripline) net should now visibly move where before it was frequency-flat.
3. Set reference back to 1 GHz → returns to baseline exactly (model is constructed to be exact at the measurement point).
4. **Roughness → ~1 µm** → outer-layer (microstrip) Z₀ dips slightly; inner layers unaffected (stripline roughness still deferred).

A sanity check on the physics: Z₀ should move only a *few percent* across 1→10 GHz — that's correct (Z₀ is weakly dispersive). If you ever want the bigger high-speed payoff — **insertion loss in dB/inch** — that's the natural next feature now that the causal Dk(f)/Df(f) + roughness + resistivity are all wired; the model already computes the loss terms, we'd just surface them.

Two open items remain (both noted in tasks): **stripline roughness** (needs the transline model extended) and, if you want it, **per-net frequency override** via tuning profiles (Altium doesn't do this, so I left it out). Want me to file the Linear ticket for this data-model workstream, or pick up loss reporting / stripline roughness next?

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## zeo

You are an AI assistant specialized in KiCad schematic and PCB design.

## Tool Overview

All schematic and PCB tools communicate with the live editor via IPC — they read and modify the in-memory state directly. The editor must be open for these tools to work. Changes made by tools are reflected immediately in the editor but are **not saved to disk** — the user saves manually with Cmd+S.

## Behavioral Guidelines

- Give progress updates — for multi-step tasks (circuit design, layout, debugging), share brief updates as you work so the user knows what's happening.
- Ask for clarification on ambiguous requests — if the user's request lacks specific component values, part numbers, or placement details, ask before proceeding
- Report errors clearly — if a tool fails, explain what went wrong and suggest fixes
- Summarize changes — after modifications, briefly state what changed (e.g., "Added R1 (10k) at 100,50")

## Workflow

1. **`check_status`** — always call first to verify which editors are open and which project is loaded. **If `is_multi_board_container == true`, see "Multi-board projects" below before doing anything else.**
2. If no project is loaded, use **`open_project`** or **`create_project`** to load one
3. If editors are closed, open the schematic and/or PCB editor
4. Use tools to inspect, add, update, delete elements
5. **`screenshot`** — take a screenshot after changes to visually verify your work
6. Run ERC/DRC to check for errors

## Multi-board projects

Some KiCad projects are *multi-board containers* — a single `.kicad_pro`
that owns several sub-projects (each its own `.kicad_pro` + `.kicad_sch` +
`.kicad_pcb`) plus a top-level multi-board schematic (`.kicad_mbs`, MBS for
short) that defines how the boards interconnect via cross-board nets.

**`check_status` tells you which kind of project is loaded:**
- `is_multi_board_container: false` → a regular single-board project. Use
  `sch_*` / `pcb_*` tools as usual; they target the one open schematic /
  PCB.

# Zeo

AI Agent extension for KiCad (open-source EDA software).

## Tech Stack

C++17, wxWidgets, libcurl, nlohmann/json

## Project Structure

```
agent/                  # AI Agent UI and LLM integration
├── agent.cpp           # Entry point (KIFACE factory)
├── agent_frame.cpp     # Main window, chat UI, event handling
├── agent_llm_client.cpp # LLM API client (OpenAI/Anthropic)
├── chat_history.cpp    # JSON persistence
├── core/
│   └── chat_controller.cpp  # Chat state machine
├── tools/
│   ├── tool_schemas.cpp         # Tool definitions (JSON schemas sent to LLM)
│   ├── tool_registry.cpp        # Singleton dispatcher (tool name → handler map)
│   ├── tool_handler.h           # Base interface for all tool handlers
│   ├── handlers/                # Tool handler implementations
│   │   ├── python_tool_handler.cpp  # Loads .py scripts, builds IPC commands (30 tools)
│   │   ├── pcb_autoroute_handler.cpp # Async Freerouting integration
│   │   └── screenshot_handler.cpp   # CLI screenshot capture
│   ├── python/                  # Python scripts (loaded at runtime)
│   │   ├── common/              # Shared utilities (preamble.py, bbox.py)
│   │   ├── schematic/           # sch_*.py (add, update, delete, connect_net, etc.)
│   │   └── pcb/                 # pcb_*.py (add, route, place, export, etc.)
│   └── util/                    # C++ helpers (kicad_cli_util)
├── auth/               # Supabase auth + keychain storage
├── bridge/             # JS↔C++ webview message router
└── view/               # Markdown→HTML, templates, file attachments

api/proto/              # Protobuf definitions for IPC API
├── schematic/          # Schematic commands
└── common/             # Shared types

eeschema/api/           # Schematic editor API handlers
├── api_handler_sch.cpp # IPC command implementations
└── api_handler_sch.h

pcbnew/                 # PCB editor
eeschema/               # Schematic editor
kicad/                  # Project manager
common/                 # Shared libraries
```

## Agent Tools Architecture

Tools follow a layered architecture:
1. **Tool Schema** (`tool_schemas.cpp`) - JSON definitions sent to LLM
2. **Tool Registry** (`tool_registry.cpp`) - Dispatches tool calls to handlers via name → handler map
3. **Tool Handler** (`python_tool_handler.cpp`) - Loads `.py` scripts and builds IPC commands
4. **IPC API** (`api_handler_sch.cpp`) - Handles protobuf commands
5. **Kipy** (`zeo-python/kipy/`) - Python bindings for IPC

For detailed process on adding/updating tools, see `/zeo-python/CLAUDE.md`

## LLM Models

The agent supports multiple Claude models. **Opus (`claude-opus-4-7`) is the preferred model** — all testing and development is done against Opus. Opus 4.6 (`claude-opus-4-6`) and Sonnet 4.6 (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) remain selectable as alternatives.

## Lint / LSP Errors

Ignore clang LSP diagnostic errors. The LSP cannot resolve CMake include paths, so it reports false positives (e.g. `'nlohmann/json.hpp' file not found`). If the build script succeeds, the code is correct.

## Debugging

Logs: `~/Library/Logs/Zeo/agent-<timestamp>.log` (one per session)

For terminal output: `WXTRACE=1 ./Zeo`

I've now read the 0.3.0 project and reviewed the branch. Here's the picture.

## Linear — Zeo 0.3.0 project state

**Done (8 impedance/variant tickets — all on this branch):**
- A1 `IMPEDANCE_TARGET_CONSTRAINT` (MOON-1417), A2 impedance DRC test provider (MOON-1423), A3 Z₀ in track props (MOON-1428), A5 Net Inspector impedance column (MOON-1430), A6 `variantIs()` (MOON-1418)
- C2a override indicator (MOON-1420), C2b BOM variant selector (MOON-1421), C2c variant-diff viewer (MOON-1422)

**In Review (3 — also on this branch):**
- A4 Z₀ in PNS router status bar (MOON-1429)
- B2 schematic diff-pair ergonomics (MOON-1425)
- C2d variant DRC consistency + indicator polish (MOON-1427)

**Backlog — the new high-speed roadmap (16 tickets, all created today 2026-05-29):** an audit-driven set grouped into:
- **XS** xSignals: XS1 data model, XS2 manual creation, XS3 classes, XS5 retarget length DRC
- **IP** impedance profiles: IP1 profile object + width synthesis, IP2 netclass "use profile", IP3 router pulls width
- **LM** length matching: LM1 match-to-longest, LM2 group-aware tuning
- **NZ** named zones: NZ1 rule-area scoping, NZ2 named stackup regions, NZ3 region-aware impedance
- **ET** extended DRC: ET1 antennae, ET2 return path, ET3 parallel segment, ET4 tuning gauge

**Other:** MOON-1357 (netclass regex), MOON-1437 (AGPL relicense), MOON-578 (canceled).

## Branch `ganesh/zeo-impedence-constraint` — changes (44 files, +1705/−9)

Two logical groups:

**1. Impedance data model (this session's work — NOT yet ticketed):**
- `board_design_settings.{h,cpp}`: 4 new `m_SI_*` params (reference freq, Dk-measurement freq, conductor resistivity, roughness), persisted under `signal_integrity.*`, defaults reproducing the old hardcoded 1 GHz/copper/smooth behavior.
- `impedance_calculator.{h,cpp}` (new): shared `IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR` with width/layer cache, dielectric-sublayer-weighted Dk/Df, microstrip/stripline split, and **Djordjevic-Sarkar causal Dk(f) dispersion** (returns datasheet values exactly at the measurement frequency, so defaults are unchanged).
- `panel_setup_impedance.{h,cpp}` (new) + `dialog_board_setup.{h,cpp}`: the Board Setup → Board Stackup → **Impedance** page editing those 4 values.

**2. The A1–A6 / B2 / C2 features (the Done + In-Review tickets):**
- DRC: `drc_rule.h`, `drc_item.{h,cpp}`, `drc_rule_parser.cpp`, `drc_rules.keywords`, `drc_engine.cpp`, `drc_test_provider_impedance.cpp` (A1/A2), `pcbexpr_functions.cpp` `variantIs()` (A6).
- UI surfaces: `dialog_track_via_properties` (A3), `pcb_net_inspector_panel*` (A5), `router_tool.{cpp,h}` Z₀ status (A4).
- Variants: `dialog_bom` (C2b), `dialog_variant_diff` (C2c), `dialog_symbol/footprint_properties` (C2a), title/toolbar indicators + `sch_edit_tool`/`sch_editor_control` diff-pair menu (C2d/B2).

The current build is clean and all three impedance phases are in. One gap worth noting: **the impedance data-model work (the `m_SI_*` params + dispersion + Impedance panel) has no Linear ticket** — it's the foundation the backlog's IP1/NZ3 build on. Want me to file it, or move on to one of the backlog tickets (IP1 is the natural next step — it promotes `TUNING_PROFILE` into a real impedance profile with width synthesis)?

{"id":"MOON-1427","title":"C2d: Variant-aware DRC consistency + discoverability polish","description":"## Summary

Round out variant UX with three smaller items: variant-consistency DRC check, status-bar active-variant indicator, and Tools > Variants menu promotion.

## Context

Per audit, three minor variant UX gaps remain after C2a–C2c:

1. DRC doesn't flag inconsistency (e.g. DNP in one variant but not another, with no explicit override)
2. No active-variant indicator outside the toolbar dropdown (easy to forget which variant you're in)
3. Variant menu is buried under Tools → Variants → …

## Implementation

### 1\. Variant consistency DRC

* `pcbnew/drc/drc_test_provider_schematic_parity.cpp:180` — extend the DNP check to validate variant consistency
* New error code `DRCE_VARIANT_INCONSISTENT`
* Fires when: a component is DNP in some variants but not others with no explicit override declaration explaining why

### 2\. Status bar indicator

* `common/eda_base_frame.cpp` (or per-frame equivalents in eeschema/pcbnew)
* Add a status-bar widget showing `Variant: [name]` (or "Default")
* Click-to-open variant selector

### 3\. Menu promotion

* `eeschema/menubar.cpp` — promote Variants from buried Tools → Variants → … to a more discoverable position
* Consider a top-level "Variants" menu if menu bar has room
* Same treatment in `pcbnew/menubar*.cpp`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] DNP-in-one-variant-only inconsistency fires a DRC warning (severity configurable in DRC settings)
- [ ] Status bar shows active variant in both eeschema and pcbnew
- [ ] Status bar indicator click opens variant selector dropdown
- [ ] Variants menu reachable in 1 click from menu bar
- [ ] No regression on existing variant operations

input.title: Impedance data model: board-level SI parameters + causal Dk(f) dispersion + setup UI
input.description:
## Summary

Replace the hardcoded impedance-calculation inputs (1 GHz / copper / smooth foil, datasheet Dk used as-is) with a real, controllable signal-integrity data model, and surface it in a Board Setup UI. This is the foundation the 0.3.1 impedance-profile (IP*) and region-aware (NZ3) work builds on.

## What shipped

### Data model — board-level SI parameters
`BOARD_DESIGN_SETTINGS` gains four analysis inputs (distinct from physical stackup geometry, which stays in `BOARD_STACKUP`), persisted to `.kicad_pro` under `signal_integrity.*`:
- `m_SI_ReferenceFrequency` — frequency Z₀/loss is evaluated at (default 1 GHz)
- `m_SI_DkMeasurementFrequency` — frequency the datasheet Dk/Df are specified at (default 1 GHz)
- `m_SI_ConductorResistivity` — Ω·m, default copper 1.72e-8 (editable for plated/heavy/non-copper)
- `m_SI_ConductorRoughness` — RMS foil roughness in m, default 0 (smooth)

Defaults reproduce the prior hardcoded behaviour exactly, so existing boards are unchanged.

### Shared impedance calculator
New `pcbnew/board_stackup_manager/impedance_calculator.{h,cpp}` — `IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR` with a layer/width cache, used by the DRC provider, track-properties dialog, router status overlay, and Net Inspector:
- Microstrip (outer) / stripline (inner) split.
- Dielectric span walk accumulates **thickness-weighted Dk/Df across all sublayers** to the reference plane, not just sublayer 0.
- Feeds real loss tangent, conductor resistivity (SIGMA = 1/ρ), and roughness into the transline model.

### Causal frequency dispersion
**Djordjevic-Sarkar (wideband-Debye) Dk(f)/Df(f)** model (transition band 1 kHz–1 THz, matching HFSS/Altium defaults). Solved so it reproduces the datasheet (Dk, Df) exactly at the measurement frequency — so the reference-frequency knob now meaningfully moves Z₀, especially on inner stripline layers where material Dk(f) is the only frequency dependence. At measurement == reference frequency it returns the inputs unchanged.

### UI
New `pcbnew/dialogs/panel_setup_impedance.{h,cpp}` — Board Setup → Board Stackup → **Impedance** page (Altium Layer-Stack-Manager analogue). Edits the four parameters with unit handling (GHz/MHz/kHz, µΩ·cm, µm).

## Verification
- Build clean on macOS.
- Set reference 1→10 GHz → Z₀ rises a few %; inner-layer net now moves where it was frequency-flat before.
- 1 GHz / 1 GHz returns the pre-change baseline exactly.
- Roughness ~1 µm dips outer-layer Z₀ slightly.

## Known follow-ups
- **Stripline roughness:** the STRIPLINE transline model's parameter map registers neither MUR nor ROUGH (SetParameter throws on unsupported keys), so roughness currently applies to microstrip only. Extend the model to register ROUGH.
- **Insertion loss (dB/inch):** the causal Dk(f)/Df(f) + roughness + resistivity are now all wired; loss terms are computed but not surfaced. Natural next high-speed payoff.
- **Per-net frequency override:** intentionally omitted — Altium uses a single board-level reference frequency.

## Files
- `include/board_design_settings.h`, `pcbnew/board_design_settings.cpp`
- `pcbnew/board_stackup_manager/impedance_calculator.{h,cpp}` (new)
- `pcbnew/dialogs/panel_setup_impedance.{h,cpp}` (new), `pcbnew/dialogs/dialog_board_setup.{cpp,h}`
- `pcbnew/CMakeLists.txt`

{"id":"MOON-1440","title":"XS1: xSignal data model — multi-net signal paths through series components","description":"## Summary

Add an `XSIGNAL` object: a designer-defined signal path that may span multiple nets bridged by series components (termination R, AC-coupling C), treated as one length-tuned electrical entity. This is the core Altium high-speed primitive and is entirely missing today.

## Context

Per audit, KiCad has **no** multi-net signal-path concept (`xsignal`/`signal_path`/series-topology searches empty). The closest is the From-To cache (`connectivity/from_to_cache.h`: `FT_PATH` with from/to pads) — but that's pad-to-pad on a **single** net. A signal net_A → R1 → net_B is two independent tuning problems today.

## Implementation

* New `XSIGNAL` object carrying:
  * Ordered list of **member nets** + the **bridging series component(s)** between them
  * **Source pad** + **target pad** (the defining endpoints)
  * Computed **length** = Σ routed member-net lengths + through-component pad-to-pad distance + optional pin/package delay contribution
* Persist with the project (alongside diff-pair / netclass storage in `PROJECT_FILE`).
* Reuse the From-To topology machinery for per-net sub-path resolution where possible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An xSignal spanning net_A → R1 → net_B reports a single total length including the through-R1 distance
- [ ] xSignal persists across save/load
- [ ] Pin/package delay (if present on the part) folds into effective length
- [ ] Length updates as member nets are routed

## Dependencies

Foundational. {"id":"MOON-1454","title":"XS5: Retarget matched-length DRC + tuning onto xSignals / classes","description":"## Summary

Wire the matched-length DRC (LM1) and the interactive tuning path so they operate on **xSignals and xSignal classes**, not just bare nets — closing the loop that makes xSignals useful for high-speed length matching across series components.

## Context

XS1 gives the signal-path object, XS3 the class. This ticket makes the length machinery consume them: an xSignal's length (incl. through-series-component distance + pin/package delay) becomes the measured quantity, and an xSignal class becomes a valid match-to-longest group scope.

## Implementation

* Matched-length DRC (LM1) accepts an xSignal class as scope; member "length" = the xSignal's full computed length (XS1), not per-net.
* Length/Matched-Length rule scope picker offers xSignal classes.
* Tuning (LM2 / meander placer) targets the xSignal's length and tunes whichever member net the user is routing, accounting for already-fixed series segments.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A matched-length rule scoped to an xSignal class matches signals that span series components
- [ ] Tuning a member net of an xSignal converges the xSignal's total length to the group target
- [ ] Through-component distance + pin/package delay included in the matched quantity
- [ ] Per-net length matching (no xSignal) still works unchanged

## Dependencies

Blocked by XS1 (<issue id="7d0c3a63-7116-4c25-83f1-2b32fae486c3">MOON-1440</issue>) + XS3 (<issue id="837228dd-f401-44fc-b2e3-442d974632cc">MOON-1449</issue>) + LM1 (<issue id="48837a67-4498-4179-abc8-cfa87fd62227">MOON-1441</issue>). \~3 d.","priority":{"value":2,"name":"High"},"url":"https://linear.app/distillmoonshine/issue/MOON-1454/xs5-retarget-matched-length-drc-tuning-onto-xsignals-classes","gitBranchName":"ganesh/moon-1454-xs5-retarget-matched-length-drc-tuning-onto-xsignals-classes","createdAt":"2026-05-29T07:28:06.348Z","updatedAt":"2026-05-29T07:47:54.434Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Feature"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Ganesh Pimpale","createdById":"4ea6e562-99b6-4d8b-ad51-653d882bcd6d","project":"Zeo 0.3.1","projectId":"e19cf80e-48d5-4bb2-bd5b-1ce25e0d90f0","team":"Moonshine","teamId":"84a83d69-1dbb-491d-9b85-7613ecfe1619"}

{"id":"MOON-1449","title":"XS3: xSignal classes (named groups)","description":"## Summary

Add `XSIGNAL_CLASS` — a named group of xSignals — so length-match rules can target a whole bus (e.g. a DDR byte lane) at once.

## Context

Altium groups xSignals into classes and scopes Matched Length rules to the class. This is the grouping layer between XS1 (the xSignal) and LM1 (match-to-longest).

## Implementation

* `XSIGNAL_CLASS { name, members[] }`, persisted with the project alongside netclasses.
* Add/remove xSignals to/from a class in the xSignals panel.
* Expose class as a scope target for DRC rules (so LM1's match-to-longest can scope to an xSignal class — wired in XS5).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Can create a named class and assign xSignals to it
- [ ] Class persists across save/load
- [ ] Class is selectable as a rule scope
- [ ] An xSignal can belong to a class; removing it updates the class

{"id":"MOON-1448","title":"XS2: Manual xSignal creation (pick source + target pad)","description":"## Summary

Let a user create an xSignal by selecting a source pad and a target pad; Zeo walks the connectivity (through series components) to build the `XSIGNAL` member-net path.

## Context

XS1 defines the object; this is the primary manual authoring path (Altium: select source pad + target pad, right-click → create xSignal).

## Implementation

* PCB selection action "Create xSignal from selected pads" (2 pads selected).
* Walk connectivity from source toward target; when a net ends at a series 2-pin part (R/C/L), cross to the part's other pad and continue; record member nets + bridging parts until the target pad.
* Name the xSignal (default from endpoints); store via XS1 persistence.
* An xSignals panel/list to view + delete (minimal; full editor can follow).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting two pads bridged by a series resistor creates one xSignal spanning both nets
- [ ] Direct (single-net) source→target also creates a valid xSignal
- [ ] Ambiguous branching path surfaces a clear message rather than guessing silently
- [ ] Created xSignals appear in a list and persist

{"id":"MOON-1441","title":"LM1: Match-to-longest length-match group constraint","description":"## Summary

Add a group length-match constraint that matches all members of a class to the **longest member within a tolerance** (Altium's Matched Length semantics: `MinLimit = longest − tolerance`), rather than checking each path against an absolute target independently.

## Context

Per audit, `drc_test_provider_matched_length.cpp` handles `LENGTH_CONSTRAINT` / `SKEW_CONSTRAINT` per From-To path independently — no group-relative matching for N>2 nets. `MEANDER_SETTINGS` has a `m_crossBoardSiblingDeltaNm` runtime cache hinting at group awareness, reusable here.

## Implementation

* New constraint flavor (or extend matched-length): `matched_length` over a scope = net class or (once XS3 lands) xSignal class.
* Evaluator: gather member lengths, find longest, flag any member below `longest − tolerance`.
* Report per-member deltas in the DRC violation detail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A rule matching a net class of 8 members flags those more than `tolerance` shorter than the longest
- [ ] Tolerance is configurable in the rule
- [ ] Violation detail lists each member's delta-to-longest
- [ ] Works on net classes now; xSignal-class scoping wired in XS5

## Dependencies

Foundational for length matching. Blocks LM2. {"id":"MOON-1450","title":"LM2: Group-aware length tuning (tune-to-longest in router)","description":"## Summary

When interactively tuning a member of a length-match group, the meander placer targets the group's longest-member length (from LM1), not a fixed per-net target — so tuning a bus converges all members to match.

## Context

Per audit, `MEANDER_SETTINGS` already has a `m_crossBoardSiblingDeltaNm` runtime cache that resolves a sibling-relative delta for cross-board tuning. Generalize that to query group siblings' current lengths and target (longest − within tolerance).

## Implementation

* In the meander placer, when the net belongs to a LM1 group, compute target = max(member lengths) and tune the active member toward it.
* Reuse / generalize the cross-board sibling-delta machinery for the sibling-length query.
* Live tuning status (too short / matched) reflects group target; surfaces in the ET4 gauge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tuning one member of an 8-net group targets the current longest member
- [ ] As the longest changes (routing other members), the target updates
- [ ] Diff-pair and single-net group members both supported
- [ ] Tuning status shows matched when within tolerance of longest

## Dependencies

Blocked by LM1 (<issue id="48837a67-4498-4179-abc8-cfa87fd62227">MOON-1441</issue>). {"id":"MOON-1453","title":"ET4: Live length/delay tuning gauge in router","description":"## Summary

Extend the router status readout with a live length/delay-to-target gauge while tuning — current routed length + estimated remaining, valid range, and under/in-range/over color feedback (Altium's tuning gauge).

## Context

Per audit, the router already shows live Z₀ (A4, `router_tool.cpp::buildImpedanceStatus`) and the meander placer already computes `TuningLengthResult()` / `TuningDelayResult()` / `TuningStatus()` (`pns_meander_placer_base.h`: TOO_SHORT/TOO_LONG/TUNED). This is mostly UX wiring to surface those continuously, including group target (LM2) and time-domain delay.

## Implementation

* Add a length/delay gauge to the router status overlay (`router_status_view_item`), driven by `TuningStatus()` + `TuningLengthResult()` / `TuningDelayResult()`.
* Show target source (rule / group-longest from LM2 / manual) and valid range.
* Color: under (short) / in-range (matched) / over (long).
* Delay shown when the net's profile has time-domain tuning enabled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tuning a net shows live current length + remaining-to-target with color state
- [ ] Group members (LM2) show target = longest sibling
- [ ] Delay displayed for time-domain-enabled nets
- [ ] No measurable routing perf regression

## Dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1452","title":"ET2: Return Path DRC rule","description":"## Summary

Add a Return Path DRC rule (Altium high-speed): for impedance-controlled nets, verify a continuous reference plane under the trace and a nearby stitching via at layer transitions.

## Context

Per audit, no return-path check exists. Altium's Return Path rule draws its reference layer(s) from the impedance profile — hence the IP1 dependency. SI-grade check.

## Implementation

* New `RETURN_PATH_CONSTRAINT` carrying: min continuous-copper gap beyond trace edge, max stitch-via distance.
* Reference layer(s) resolved from the net's impedance profile (IP1) top/bottom ref.
* `DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_RETURN_PATH`: along each scoped track, check the reference layer has continuous copper within the gap; at layer transitions (vias), check for a return/stitch via within max distance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A trace crossing a plane split/gap on its reference layer raises a violation
- [ ] A layer-transition via with no nearby return via raises a violation
- [ ] Reference layer correctly taken from the impedance profile
- [ ] Unit test in `qa/tests/pcbnew/`

## Dependencies

Blocked by IP1 (<issue id="eab89f68-5dc2-4b20-9d25-83170fd0e6d8">MOON-1439</issue>) for the reference-layer source. \~3 d.","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/distillmoonshine/issue/MOON-1452/et2-return-path-drc-rule","gitBranchName":"ganesh/moon-1452-et2-return-path-drc-rule","createdAt":"2026-05-29T07:27:40.398Z","updatedAt":"2026-05-29T07:48:08.396Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Feature"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Ganesh Pimpale","createdById":"4ea6e562-99b6-4d8b-ad51-653d882bcd6d","project":"Zeo 0.3.1","projectId":"e19cf80e-48d5-4bb2-bd5b-1ce25e0d90f0","team":"Moonshine","teamId":"84a83d69-1dbb-491d-9b85-7613ecfe1619"}

{"id":"MOON-1439","title":"IP1: Impedance profile object + per-layer width/gap synthesis","description":"## Summary

Promote the existing `TUNING_PROFILE` into a first-class **impedance profile**: target Z₀ + tolerance, profile type (single / differential / coplanar), and per-layer **synthesized** trace width (and gap for diff) computed from the stackup. This is the prescriptive half of impedance control — "specify 50 Ω, get the width" — complementing the read-only impedance DRC shipped in A1/A2.

## Build on what exists

Per audit, `include/project/tuning_profiles.h` already has `TUNING_PROFILE { m_ProfileName, m_Type (SINGLE|DIFFERENTIAL), m_TargetImpedance, per-layer DELAY_PROFILE_TRACK_PROPAGATION_ENTRY { signalLayer, top/bottomReferenceLayer, width, diffPairGap, delay } }`. This is \~90% of an Altium impedance profile but is used only by the tuning UI. `common/transline_calculations/microstrip.h` exposes `SynthesizeWidth()` (width from target Z₀ + dielectric) — currently uncalled for design synthesis.

## Implementation

* Extend the profile object (or factor a shared `IMPEDANCE_PROFILE` base) to carry `m_TargetTolerance` and mark per-layer width/gap as **synthesized** outputs.
* On profile edit / stackup change, call `SynthesizeWidth()` per signal layer using `BOARD_STACKUP` Dk/Df + reference-layer distances; populate width (+ gap for diff) per layer.
* Bidirectional: editing a width back-solves Z₀ (mirror Altium).
* Persist with the project (profiles already persist via tuning profiles).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A profile with target 50 Ω single-ended populates a synthesized width per signal layer from the current stackup
- [ ] A differential 90/100 Ω profile populates width + gap per layer
- [ ] Editing width back-solves and displays the resulting Z₀
- [ ] Synthesis matches the existing impedance DRC's Z₀ calc for the same geometry (round-trip consistency)

## Dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1446","title":"IP2: Netclass / Width rule "Use Impedance Profile"","description":"## Summary

Let a netclass (and the track-width rule) be driven by an impedance profile: when "use profile" is set, per-layer track width (and diff-pair gap) come from the profile's synthesized values instead of fixed numbers. Mirrors Altium's "Use Impedance Profile" on the Width / Diff-Pair Routing rules.

## Context

Per audit, `NETCLASS` (netclass.h) already references a tuning profile by name (`GetTuningProfile()`) and carries diff-pair width/gap as `std::optional<int>` with inheritance. IP1 turns that profile into a width source.

## Implementation

* Add a "use impedance profile" flag + profile reference to the netclass / width-rule resolution.
* When set, netclass `GetTrackWidth(layer)` / diff-pair width+gap resolve from the IP1 profile's per-layer synthesized values; Min/Max stay editable, Preferred becomes profile-driven (Altium behavior).
* Falls back to fixed netclass values when no profile assigned.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A netclass with an assigned profile yields per-layer widths from the profile
- [ ] Diff-pair width + gap likewise driven on a differential profile
- [ ] Netclasses without a profile behave exactly as today
- [ ] Changing the stackup re-derives widths via IP1

## Dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1447","title":"IP3: Router pulls trace width from impedance profile per layer","description":"## Summary

During interactive routing, when the active net has an impedance profile, the router uses the profile's synthesized width for the current layer automatically (and switches width on layer change). Pairs with the live Z₀ readout from A4.

## Context

Per audit, the router already reads net width via the rule resolver (`pns_kicad_iface.cpp`) and shows live Z₀ (A4, `router_tool.cpp::buildImpedanceStatus`). This makes width follow the profile so the routed trace actually hits the target Z₀ as the user changes layers.

## Implementation

* In the PNS sizing path, when the net's netclass has an impedance profile (IP2), set `Sizes().TrackWidth()` from the profile's synthesized width for `GetCurrentLayer()`.
* On layer switch mid-route, re-pull width for the new layer.
* Keep manual width override possible (profile = default, not a lock).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Routing an impedance-controlled net auto-selects the profile width for the start layer
- [ ] Switching layers mid-route updates the width to that layer's synthesized value
- [ ] A4 Z₀ readout reflects the target after the auto-width
- [ ] Non-profile nets route with current behavior

## Dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1442","title":"NZ1: Rule-area scoping — insideArea() / intersectsArea() expression functions","description":"## Summary

Let DRC rules scope to a **named rule area** (the "rule areas" half of named zones), so a rule like the impedance target can be bound to a region: `(condition "insideArea('HighSpeed')")`.

## Context

Per audit, `ZONE` with `m_isRuleArea` (zone.h:715–735) is keepout/placement only — there is no way to scope a DRC rule to a named region. We added a directly analogous mechanism in A6 (`variantIs()` in `pcbexpr_evaluator.cpp` / `pcbexpr_functions.cpp`); mirror that pattern.

## Implementation

* Ensure rule areas carry a user-facing **name** field (add if missing).
* Add `insideArea('name')` (item fully inside) and `intersectsArea('name')` (item touches) expression functions in `pcbnew/pcbexpr_functions.cpp`, evaluated against the named rule-area polygon(s).
* Register in the expression function registry (same path as `variantIs`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A rule with `(condition "insideArea('HighSpeed')")` applies only to items inside that named area
- [ ] `intersectsArea` variant works for items crossing the boundary
- [ ] Unknown area name → rule simply never matches (no crash)
- [ ] Unit test in `qa/tests/pcbnew/`

## Dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1443","title":"NZ2: Named stackup regions data model","description":"## Summary

Extend `BOARD_STACKUP` so a board can carry **named regions**, each with its own ordered layer stack + dielectrics (the "stackup regions" half of named zones). Data model only — foldable 3D rendering stays in 0.5.0.

## Context

Per audit, `pcbnew/board_stackup_manager/board_stackup.h` is a flat list of layers with per-dielectric Dk/Df/thickness (`DIELECTRIC_PRMS`), no regions. This is the foundation for region-aware impedance (NZ3) now and rigid-flex later.

## Implementation

* Add a `STACKUP_REGION { name, boundary (polygon or board-area ref), BOARD_STACKUP subStack }` collection to the board.
* A default full-board region preserves today's single-stack behavior (back-compat: a board with no explicit regions behaves exactly as now).
* Persistence in `.kicad_pcb` with a schema bump; round-trips through save/load.
* Region boundaries can reference a named rule area (ties into NZ1) or carry their own polygon.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A board can define ≥2 named regions, each with a distinct layer stack
- [ ] Default (no regions declared) board loads/saves identically to current behavior
- [ ] Regions persist across save/load with schema migration for old files
- [ ] API to resolve "which region contains point P / item I"

## Dependencies

Foundational for rigid-flex. Blocks NZ3. {"id":"MOON-1451","title":"NZ3: Region-aware impedance resolution","description":"## Summary

Make impedance profile resolution (IP1) region-aware: a track's Z₀ / synthesized width is computed against the stackup of the **named region** (NZ2) it sits in, not a single global stack. Required for correct impedance once a board has multiple stackup regions (rigid-flex, mixed-stack).

## Context

Ties NZ2 (named stackup regions) to IP1 (impedance profiles). Without this, impedance math assumes one global stack and is wrong inside a region with a different layer set.

## Implementation

* Impedance calc + `SynthesizeWidth()` (IP1) take the region's sub-stack, resolved via NZ2's "which region contains item" API.
* The impedance DRC provider (A2) and router width (IP3) both route their stackup lookups through the region resolver.
* Default (single-region) board behaves exactly as IP1 alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A track in region A and an identical-width track in region B (different stacks) compute different Z₀
- [ ] Impedance DRC uses the correct per-region stack
- [ ] Router auto-width uses the region's stack at the cursor
- [ ] Single-region boards unchanged

## Dependencies

Blocked by NZ2 (<issue id="ea2a7f63-86c1-4320-8558-1d721429bba1">MOON-1443</issue>) + IP1 (<issue id="eab89f68-5dc2-4b20-9d25-83170fd0e6d8">MOON-1439</issue>). \~2 d.","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/distillmoonshine/issue/MOON-1451/nz3-region-aware-impedance-resolution","gitBranchName":"ganesh/moon-1451-nz3-region-aware-impedance-resolution","createdAt":"2026-05-29T07:27:34.292Z","updatedAt":"2026-05-29T07:48:21.508Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Feature"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Ganesh Pimpale","createdById":"4ea6e562-99b6-4d8b-ad51-653d882bcd6d","project":"Zeo 0.3.1","projectId":"e19cf80e-48d5-4bb2-bd5b-1ce25e0d90f0","team":"Moonshine","teamId":"84a83d69-1dbb-491d-9b85-7613ecfe1619"}

{"id":"MOON-1444","title":"ET1: Net Antennae DRC rule","description":"## Summary

Add a Net Antennae DRC rule that flags dangling routing stubs (track segments connected at only one end — "antennae") beyond an allowed length, an Altium high-speed check.

## Context

Per audit, no antennae check exists. New constraint type + test provider, following the established pattern (enum in `pcbnew/drc/drc_rule.h`, keyword in `common/drc_rules.keywords`, parse case in `drc_rule_parser.cpp`, new `drc_test_provider_*` with `DRC_REGISTER_TEST_PROVIDER`).

## Implementation

* New `ANTENNA_CONSTRAINT` (allowed dangling-stub length, default 0 = any antenna flagged).
* New `DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_ANTENNA`: walk connectivity, find track ends connected to nothing (not a pad/via/junction), measure dangling run length, flag if > allowed.
* New `DRCE_DANGLING_TRACK` / antenna error code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A track stub connected at only one end longer than the allowed length raises a violation
- [ ] Deliberately-stubbed test points (below threshold) don't false-positive
- [ ] Severity configurable in DRC settings
- [ ] Unit test in `qa/tests/pcbnew/`

## Dependencies

{"id":"MOON-1445","title":"ET3: Parallel Segment (crosstalk) DRC rule","description":"## Summary

Add a Parallel Segment DRC rule (Altium high-speed): flag two nets running parallel within a gap threshold for more than a max parallel length — a crosstalk guard.

## Context

Per audit, no crosstalk/parallel-run check exists. Same new-constraint pattern as ET1.

## Implementation

* New `PARALLEL_SEGMENT_CONSTRAINT` carrying: gap threshold (within which parallelism counts), max allowed parallel length, optional scope (e.g. between two net classes / aggressor-victim).
* New `DRC_TEST_PROVIDER_PARALLEL_SEGMENT`: for scoped track pairs, compute parallel-run length where edge-to-edge gap ≤ threshold; flag runs exceeding the max.
* Use the board RTree for candidate-pair narrowing (pattern from `drc_test_provider_disallow.cpp` spatial query).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two parallel tracks within the gap threshold for longer than the max length raise a violation
- [ ] Brief crossings / short adjacencies below the max don't false-positive
- [ ] Rule scopable to specific nets/classes (aggressor vs victim)
- [ ] Unit test in `qa/tests/pcbnew/`

## Dependencies

content.text:
Good instinct to check — this is the key accuracy question for the model. Here's the honest picture.

## What the PCB Calculator offers vs. what we use

The standalone **PCB Calculator** app exposes 9 transline types (`transline_ident.cpp`): microstrip, coplanar, grounded coplanar, stripline, coupled microstrip, coupled stripline, rectangular waveguide, coax, twisted pair.

But our impedance work doesn't use that app's code. It uses the **shared `common/transline_calculations/` library**, which only has **4** models: `microstrip`, `stripline`, `coupled_microstrip`, `coupled_stripline`.

And our `IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR` (impedance_calculator.cpp:301) currently uses just **2 of those 4**, selected by a single rule:

```cpp
if( aLayer == F_Cu || aLayer == B_Cu )   → analyseMicrostrip(...)
else                                      → analyseStripline(...)
```

So: **outer layer ⇒ microstrip, any inner layer ⇒ stripline.** That's the entire decision. One assumption per layer position, single-ended only.

## What that means — the real gaps

The non-PCB models (coax, waveguide, twisted pair) are correctly irrelevant. The ones that *matter* and we don't handle:

1. **Differential pairs (coupled microstrip/stripline).** We explicitly punt — the header even says diff-pair Z₀ is out of scope. A USB/LVDS/DDR pair gets each track scored as if it were an isolated single-ended trace, ignoring coupling. This is the biggest gap, and it's exactly what **IP1 (MOON-1439)** in 0.3.1 is meant to fix (the profile carries `DIFFERENTIAL` type + gap).

2. **Coplanar / grounded-coplanar waveguide (GCPW).** Very common in high-speed/RF: a signal trace with ground pour on both sides at a defined gap. The side grounds substantially lower Z₀. We always model it as plain microstrip/stripline and ignore adjacent coplanar grounds entirely — so for GCPW routing our number will read **high**. The library has no coplanar model at all, so this needs porting from the PCB-calc `coplanar.cpp`.

3. **Asymmetric stripline.** We *do* pass the offset (`STRIPLINE_A` = top dielectric height), so an off-center stripline is handled. Good.

4. **Embedded/covered microstrip** (soldermask dielectric above the trace). Minor — a fraction of an ohm. We treat outer traces as bare microstrip (air above). Acceptable approximation.

5. **Stripline roughness** — already a tracked follow-up; the STRIPLINE model doesn't register ROUGH.

## Bottom line

For **single-ended traces on a normal plane-referenced stack**, the microstrip/stripline split is the right and standard choice — that's what we built and it's accurate. The two situations where we'll be **meaningfully wrong** are **differential pairs** and **coplanar-referenced traces**, because we have no model selected for them.

Given you want to close out 0.3.0: differential is already deferred to IP1 in 0.3.1, which is the correct home for it (it needs the profile/gap data model anyway). The question for *this* milestone is coplanar — do you want me to note these scope boundaries on the MOON-1456 ticket so the assumption is documented, and/or pull coplanar handling in now?

Want me to:

questions.question: How should we handle the model-coverage gaps (differential + coplanar) for closing 0.3.0?

options.label: Document on MOON-1456, defer both

options.label: Add coplanar/GCPW detection now
options.description: Detect adjacent coplanar ground + gap and use a coplanar model in 0.3.0. Larger — the shared library has no coplanar model, so it needs porting from pcb_calculator/coplanar.cpp first.

102	class TRANSLINE_CALCULATION_BASE
103	{
104	public:
105	    /**
106	    * Constructs the transmission line calculation object.
107	    *
108	    * @aParameters all parameters that are used (as inputs or outputs) by the calculation
109	    */
110	    TRANSLINE_CALCULATION_BASE( std::initializer_list<TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS> aParameters )
111	    {
112	        InitProperties( aParameters );
113	    }
114	
115	    virtual ~TRANSLINE_CALCULATION_BASE() {}
116	
117	    /// Sets the given calculation property
118	    void SetParameter( const TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS aParam, const double aValue ) { m_parameters.at( aParam ) = aValue; }
119	
120	    /// Gets the given calculation property
121	    double GetParameter( const TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS aParam ) const { return m_parameters.at( aParam ); }
122	
123	    /// Adds a constant to the given parameter
124	    double& GetParameterRef( const TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS aParam ) { return m_parameters[aParam]; }
125	
126	    /// Gets the output parameters following analysis
127	    std::unordered_map<TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS, std::pair<double, TRANSLINE_STATUS>>& GetAnalysisResults();
128	
129	    /// Gets the output parameters following synthesis
130	    std::unordered_map<TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS, std::pair<double, TRANSLINE_STATUS>>& GetSynthesisResults();
131	
132	    /// Analyses the transmission line using the current parameter set
133	    virtual void Analyse() = 0;
134	
135	    /// Synthesis the transmission line using the current parameter set target
136	    /// @returns true if the synthesis converged, otherwise false
137	    virtual bool Synthesize( SYNTHESIZE_OPTS aOpts ) = 0;
138	
139	protected:
140	    /// Initialises the properties used (as inputs or outputs) by the calculation
141	    void InitProperties( const std::initializer_list<TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS>& aParams );
142	
143	    /// Sets values in the output analysis results structure
144	    virtual void SetAnalysisResults() = 0;
145	
146	    /// Sets values in the output synthesis results structure
147	    virtual void SetSynthesisResults() = 0;
148	
149	    /// Sets an analysis result
150	    void SetAnalysisResult( TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS aParam, const double aValue,
151	                            const TRANSLINE_STATUS aStatus = TRANSLINE_STATUS::OK );
152	
153	    /// Sets a synthesis result
154	    void SetSynthesisResult( TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS aParam, const double aValue,
155	                             const TRANSLINE_STATUS aStatus = TRANSLINE_STATUS::OK );
156	
157	    /**
158	     * minimizeZ0Error1D
159	     *
160	     * Tries to find a parameter that minimizes the error on Z0.
161	     * This function only works with a single parameter.
162	     * Calls @ref Analyse several times until the error is acceptable.
163	     *
164	     * This function does not change Z0 / Angl_L
165	     *
166	     * @param aOptimise Parameter to optimise
167	     * @param aMeasure The parameter to measure / optimise against
168	     * @param aRecalculateLength True if the angular length should be recalculated (not for differential pair usage)
169	     * @returns true if error < MAX_ERROR, otherwise false
170	     */
171	    bool MinimiseZ0Error1D( TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS aOptimise, TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS aMeasure,
172	                            bool aRecalculateLength = false );
173	
174	    /**
175	     * minimizeZ0Error2D
176	     *
177	     * Tries to find the parameters that minimizes the error on Z_Diff.
178	     * This function only works with two parameters.
179	     * Calls @ref Analyse several times until the error is acceptable.
180	     * While the error is unacceptable, changes slightly the parameter.
181	     *
182	     * This function does not change Z0 / Angl_L
183	     *
184	     * @param aParam1 First parameter to optimise
185	     * @param aParam2 Secpmd parameter to optimise
186	     * @returns true if error < MAX_ERROR, otherwise false
187	     */
188	    bool MinimiseZ0Error2D( TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS aParam1, TRANSLINE_PARAMETERS aParam2 );
189	
190	    /**
191	    * Calculate skin depth
192	    *
193	    * \f$ \frac{1}{\sqrt{ \pi \cdot f \cdot \mu \cdot \sigma }} \f$
194	    */
195	    double SkinDepth() const;
196	
197	    /**
198	    * Calculates the unit propagation delay (ps/cm) for the given effective permittivity
199	    *
200	    * @aEpsilonEff is the effective permittivity of the material
201	    */
202	    static double UnitPropagationDelay( double aEpsilonEff );
203	
204	    /**
205	     * Computes the complete elliptic integral of first kind K() and the second kind E() using the
206	     * arithmetic-geometric mean algorithm (AGM) by Abramowitz and Stegun.
207	     *
208	     * @returns std::pair<K, E> where K = first kind integral, E = second kind integral
209	     */

36	 * m_SI_* fields by the BOARD overload of ComputeOhms().
37	 */
38	struct IMPEDANCE_PARAMS
39	{
40	    double frequencyHz         = 1.0e9;    ///< analysis frequency (modal dispersion + skin depth)
41	    double dkMeasurementFreqHz = 1.0e9;    ///< frequency the stackup Dk/Df are specified at
42	    double conductorRho        = 1.72e-8;  ///< conductor resistivity, ohm-metre (copper @20°C)

47	/**
48	 * Single-ended characteristic impedance Z₀ calculation for tracks on a copper layer.
49	 *
50	 * Microstrip is used for outer copper layers (F.Cu / B.Cu); stripline for inner copper
51	 * layers (dielectric on both sides).  Differential pair impedance is intentionally out
52	 * of scope here — that uses COUPLED_MICROSTRIP / COUPLED_STRIPLINE and is handled
53	 * separately.
54	 *
55	 * The calculator is intentionally stateless apart from a width/layer → Z₀ cache, so it
56	 * can be embedded in the DRC test provider, the track properties dialog, the PNS router
57	 * status overlay, and the Net Inspector — all of which need the same number.
58	 */
59	class IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR
60	{
61	public:
62	    IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR() = default;
63	
64	    /**
65	     * Compute Z₀ in ohms for a given (layer, track-width-in-IU) pair using the board's
66	     * active stackup.  Returns 0 if the stackup is incomplete or the layer/width pair
67	     * cannot be analysed.
68	     *
69	     * Results are cached per-instance; call ClearCache() when the stackup may have
70	     * changed.
71	     */
72	    int ComputeOhms( BOARD* aBoard, PCB_LAYER_ID aLayer, int aWidthIU );
73	
74	    /**
75	     * Same as ComputeOhms but accepts a pre-fetched stackup so callers iterating many
76	     * tracks don't pay the per-call GetStackupOrDefault() cost.  Uses the SI params most
77	     * recently set via SetParams() (default: legacy 1 GHz / copper / smooth).
78	     */
79	    int ComputeOhms( const BOARD_STACKUP& aStackup, PCB_LAYER_ID aLayer, int aWidthIU );
80	
81	    /// Set the signal-integrity analysis parameters (frequency, conductor properties).
82	    /// Clears the cache, since cached results depend on these.
83	    void SetParams( const IMPEDANCE_PARAMS& aParams )
84	    {
85	        m_params = aParams;
86	        m_cache.clear();
87	    }
88	
89	    const IMPEDANCE_PARAMS& GetParams() const { return m_params; }
90	
91	    void ClearCache() { m_cache.clear(); }
92

94	    struct CACHE_KEY
95	    {
96	        PCB_LAYER_ID layer;
97	        int          width;
98	
99	        bool operator==( const CACHE_KEY& o ) const { return layer == o.layer && width == o.width; }
100	    };
101	
102	    struct CACHE_KEY_HASH
103	    {
104	        std::size_t operator()( const CACHE_KEY& k ) const noexcept
105	        {

107	                   ^ ( std::hash<int>{}( k.width ) << 1 );

114	};

input.description:
## Summary

Replace the hardcoded impedance-calculation inputs (1 GHz / copper / smooth foil, datasheet Dk used as-is) with a real, controllable signal-integrity data model; surface it in a Board Setup UI; and select the correct transmission-line model per track (single-ended, differential, or coplanar).

## What shipped

### Data model — board-level SI parameters
`BOARD_DESIGN_SETTINGS` gains four analysis inputs (distinct from physical stackup geometry, which stays in `BOARD_STACKUP`), persisted to `.kicad_pro` under `signal_integrity.*`:
- `m_SI_ReferenceFrequency` — frequency Z₀/loss is evaluated at (default 1 GHz)
- `m_SI_DkMeasurementFrequency` — frequency the datasheet Dk/Df are specified at (default 1 GHz)
- `m_SI_ConductorResistivity` — Ω·m, default copper 1.72e-8
- `m_SI_ConductorRoughness` — RMS foil roughness in m, default 0

Defaults reproduce the prior behaviour exactly.

### Shared impedance calculator + model selection
`pcbnew/board_stackup_manager/impedance_calculator.{h,cpp}` — `IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR`, used by the DRC provider, track-properties dialog, router status overlay, and Net Inspector. Two entry points:
- `ComputeOhms()` — fast single-ended Z₀ from (layer, width); cached.
- **`ComputeForTrack(board, track)`** — board/track aware; picks the model per track and returns `{singleEndedOhms, differentialOhms, model}`:
  - **Differential pair** → coupled microstrip (outer) / coupled stripline (inner), reporting Z_diff. Detected via `BOARD::DpCoupledNet()`; gap measured to the nearest same-layer segment of the coupled net.

content.text:
Done. The calculator now selects three model families automatically, and it's built and installed.

## What changed

**New model in the shared library** — `common/transline_calculations/coplanar.{h,cpp}`: I ported the CPW + grounded-CPW (CPWG) quasi-static/dispersion model from the PCB Calculator into the `TRANSLINE_CALCULATION_BASE` framework. The library previously only had microstrip/stripline and their coupled variants.

**`IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR::ComputeForTrack(board, track)`** — picks the model per track and returns `{singleEndedOhms, differentialOhms, model}`:
- **Differential pair** → coupled microstrip/stripline (reports **Z_diff**). Detected via `BOARD::DpCoupledNet()`; gap measured to the nearest same-layer segment of the coupled net.
- **Coplanar (CPWG)** → the new model. Detected **conservatively**: ground copper on *both* sides within ~3 trace widths (≤1 mm) of the trace edge, roughly symmetric — otherwise it falls back to microstrip/stripline, so ordinary plane-referenced traces are unchanged.
- **Single-ended** → microstrip/stripline (the original path, still cached via `ComputeOhms`).

**Wired into all three surfaces:** DRC now checks the **differential** target for diff pairs; Track Properties shows "Differential Z" / "Z₀ (CPW)" labels when applicable; Net Inspector's average column is model-aware.

So to answer your original question directly: before, it was a single assumption per layer (outer=microstrip, inner=stripline). Now it accounts for the three PCB-relevant families. The PCB Calculator's remaining types — coax, rectangular waveguide, twisted pair — aren't board structures, so they're intentionally excluded.

## One thing to be aware of when testing

**Coplanar auto-detection is a geometric heuristic.** It triggers only on symmetric ground copper on both sides within a tight window, biased to avoid misclassifying normal microstrip. The tradeoff: it may *under*-detect a coplanar trace whose grounds are asymmetric or further out (→ safely falls back to microstrip). The definitive, explicit coplanar control belongs to the IP1 impedance-profile "CPW type" in 0.3.1; the window/symmetry constants are documented in `impedance_calculator.cpp` if you want them looser.

## Test path
1. **Diff pair** (e.g. USB `D+`/`D-`): with both tracks routed, open Track Properties on one → row reads **"Differential Z: ~90"** (not the single-ended number). Net Inspector shows the diff value on both rows. An `impedance_target` rule on the pair now checks against that diff value.
2. **CPWG trace**: a trace flanked by GND pour on both sides → Track Properties reads **"Impedance Z₀ (CPW): …"**, lower than the equivalent microstrip.
3. **Normal trace**: unchanged microstrip/stripline number — confirms no regression.

MOON-1456 is updated to document the expanded coverage and the coplanar-detection caveat. Want me to verify on a specific board, or move on to the next 0.3.0 item?

**1. Insertion loss across every model** — the calculator now computes conductor (skin + roughness) and dielectric (tan δ) loss for microstrip, stripline, coplanar, and both coupled models. `IMPEDANCE_RESULT` carries `conductorLossDbPerInch` / `dielectricLossDbPerInch` / `totalLossDbPerInch()`.

Consistent roughness** — the Hammerstad-Jensen conductor-loss correction `1 + (2/π)·atan(1.4·(Δ/δ)²)` is now applied to **stripline, coplanar, and coupled-stripline** (microstrip/coupled-microstrip already did it internally). So the copper-roughness knob affects loss on *every* model now — that was the original "stripline roughness" gap.

**3. Coupled-stripline loss** — that model emits no loss terms, so per-line loss is derived from an equivalent centered single stripline (same width, full plate separation) plus analytic dielectric loss.

**4. UI** — Track Properties gained an **"Insertion loss … dB/in"** readout (shown for a single selected track, model-aware).

## What still genuinely remains (not quick patches)

These are the items that need real new work rather than a patch, and I deliberately did **not** fake them:

1. **Asymmetric / offset coupled stripline** — `COUPLED_STRIPLINE` is mathematically a *symmetric* (centered) Cohn model. An offset coupled-stripline needs a different numerical solver. Real new model, not a patch.
2. **Coplanar detection stays a geometric heuristic** — by design conservative; the definitive explicit "this net is CPW" control is **IP1's profile type in 0.3.1**.
3. **Router live readout is single-ended only** — diff/coplanar-aware mid-route feedback is **ET4/IP3 in 0.3.1** (the partner/gap often isn't placed yet while routing).
4. **Net Inspector loss column** — the impedance column is model-aware; I didn't add a separate per-net loss column (optional, and loss is more a per-segment metric).

Items 2–4 are already represented by 0.3.1 tickets; item 1 is the only thing without a home — I can file it if you want it tracked.

## Test path for the new bits
- **Loss:** open Track Properties on a single track → **Insertion loss** shows dB/in. Raise the board **reference frequency** (Board Setup → Impedance) → loss climbs (∝√f conductor + ∝f dielectric). Raise **roughness** → conductor loss climbs on all layers now, not just outer.
- **Regression:** roughness 0 / 1 GHz → same Z₀ and small loss as before.

MOON-1456 has a comment documenting exactly what's closed vs. remaining. The model now covers single-ended / differential / coplanar **with loss and roughness consistently** — that's a robust impedance model for the practical PCB cases. Want me to file the asymmetric-coupled-stripline follow-up, or move to verifying A4/B2 to finish closing 0.3.0?

input.title: Offset / asymmetric coupled stripline impedance model
input.description:
## Problem

`COUPLED_STRIPLINE` (`common/transline_calculations/coupled_stripline.cpp`) implements only the **symmetric (centred) shielded coupled-strip** case (Cohn 1954/1955). For a differential pair on an inner layer that is **not** centred between its reference planes, the computed Z_diff is wrong — and `IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR::ComputeForTrack()` currently forces the symmetric assumption (`H = top + bot + t`, no offset). It also emits **no loss terms** and registers neither `TAND` nor `ROUGH`, so today the calculator estimates coupled-stripline loss from an *equivalent centred single stripline* (a workaround, not a real coupled-line loss model).

## What needs to be upgraded

1. **Add an offset-capable coupled stripline model.** Either extend `COUPLED_STRIPLINE` to accept `STRIPLINE_A` (offset of the strip plane from the nearer reference plane, as single `STRIPLINE` already does) or add a `COUPLED_STRIPLINE_OFFSET` class. Reference formulations: Cohn shielded coupled-strip with offset correction, or Wadell, *Transmission Line Design Handbook*, §3 (offset broadside / edge-coupled stripline). Edge-coupled (side-by-side, our diff-pair case) with vertical offset is the primary target.
2. **Native loss.** Register `TAND` + `ROUGH` in the model's parameter map and emit `ATTEN_COND_ODD/EVEN` + `ATTEN_DILECTRIC_ODD/EVEN` (mirror `COUPLED_MICROSTRIP`), with the Hammerstad-Jensen roughness correction applied internally — removing the equivalent-single-stripline loss workaround in `impedance_calculator.cpp`.
3. **Wire into the calculator.** In `ComputeForTrack()`'s coupled-stripline branch, pass the real top/bottom dielectric heights (offset) instead of forcing symmetry; read odd-mode loss from the model.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A pair offset toward one plane computes a Z_diff that differs measurably from the centred case and matches a reference (Polar/Wadell) within a few %.
- [ ] Centred case reproduces today's value (regression).
- [ ] Coupled-stripline loss comes from the model (odd-mode), roughness-corrected — workaround removed.
- [ ] Unit test in `qa/` comparing centred + offset against reference values.

## Notes
This is a genuinely new numerical model, not a patch — split out of the MOON-1456 robustness pass. ~3 d.

input.title: Robust coplanar (CPW/CPWG) detection + native roughness/asymmetric-gap in coplanar model
input.description:
## Problem

Coplanar handling shipped in MOON-1456 has two rough edges:

1. **Detection is a conservative geometric heuristic** (`findCoplanarGround()` in `impedance_calculator.cpp`): it only looks at **filled zones** on the same layer, requires copper within ~3×width / 1 mm on **both** sides with rough symmetry, and averages the two gaps. It ignores ground copper made of **tracks / pads / pours on different nets**, mis-handles **asymmetric** gaps (just averages), and has no notion of "is this net actually a ground reference."
2. **The ported `COPLANAR` model ignores `ROUGH`** — roughness is applied externally as a loss multiplier in the calculator rather than inside the model, and the model assumes equal gaps on both sides.

## What needs to be upgraded

**Detection (`impedance_calculator.cpp`):**
- Query same-layer copper via the board's connectivity / `DRC_RTREE` rather than only `Zones()`, so track/pad ground fills count.
- Identify a *reference* net (zero-net fill, or a net flagged as power/ground) rather than "any different net."
- Handle asymmetric left/right gaps explicitly (carry both gaps; see model change below) instead of averaging.
- Make the detection window + symmetry tolerance tunable (advanced config or BDS SI section) instead of hard-coded constants.

**Model (`common/transline_calculations/coplanar.{h,cpp}`):**
- Apply the surface-roughness correction to conductor loss **inside** the model (consume `ROUGH`), so coplanar matches the other models natively and the external multiplier in the calculator is removed.
- Optionally support unequal ground gaps (asymmetric CPW) — extend the formulation or document the symmetric-gap assumption.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A CPW trace referenced by ground *tracks/pour* (not a zone) is detected.
- [ ] Asymmetric-gap CPW resolves without averaging away the difference (or is explicitly documented).
- [ ] No misclassification of ordinary microstrip with an incidental nearby pour (regression on a plain board → still microstrip).
- [ ] Roughness affects coplanar conductor loss from within the model.
- [ ] Detection window/tolerance configurable.

## Notes
Explicit, profile-driven CPW selection (user declares "this net is CPW") is **IP1's** job in 0.3.1 (<related>MOON-1439</related>); this ticket makes the *automatic geometric* path robust for 0.3.0. ~2.5 d.

input.title: Router live readout: differential + coplanar aware Z (and loss)
input.description:
## Problem

The PNS router's live impedance readout (`router_tool.cpp::buildImpedanceStatus`, shipped as A4 / MOON-1429) calls the **single-ended** `IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR::ComputeOhms()` only. While routing a differential pair it shows a single-ended Z₀ instead of Z_diff, and over coplanar ground it shows microstrip/stripline Z. It also doesn't surface the now-available insertion loss.

## What needs to be upgraded

- **Differential routing:** when the router is in diff-pair mode, the PNS placer already knows the pair and the gap (`PNS::DIFF_PAIR` / sizes). Feed width + gap into the coupled model (`analyseCoupled*`) and display **Z_diff** live. (`ComputeForTrack` can't be used directly mid-route because the partner track isn't committed — drive the coupled calc from the router's in-progress pair geometry instead.)
- **Coplanar:** run the coplanar ground detection against the in-progress head position / layer so a CPW route reports CPW Z.
- **Loss:** add insertion loss (dB/in, from `IMPEDANCE_RESULT`) to the status overlay alongside Z.
- Factor a small shared helper so the router and `ComputeForTrack` share the model-selection logic rather than duplicating it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Routing a diff pair shows live **Z_diff**; single-ended nets unchanged.
- [ ] Routing a CPW-referenced trace shows CPW Z.
- [ ] Live insertion loss shown.
- [ ] No measurable routing-performance regression.

## Notes
Distinct from but related to ET4 (live length/delay gauge, <related><issue id="..." >MOON-1453</issue></related>, 0.3.1). This is the impedance/loss half for 0.3.0. ~2 d.

The PNS router's live impedance readout (`router_tool.cpp::buildImpedanceStatus`, shipped as A4 / <issue id="3d0dc554-b5ef-44e8-b58e-44cbe6c16dbd">MOON-1429</issue>) calls the **single-ended** `IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR::ComputeOhms()` only. While routing a differential pair it shows a single-ended Z₀ instead of Z_diff, and over coplanar ground it shows microstrip/stripline Z. It also doesn't surface the now-available insertion loss.

## What needs to be upgraded

* **Differential routing:** when the router is in diff-pair mode, the PNS placer already knows the pair and the gap (`PNS::DIFF_PAIR` / sizes). Feed width + gap into the coupled model (`analyseCoupled*`) and display **Z_diff** live. (`ComputeForTrack` can't be used directly mid-route because the partner track isn't committed — drive the coupled calc from the router's in-progress pair geometry instead.)
* **Coplanar:** run the coplanar ground detection against the in-progress head position / layer so a CPW route reports CPW Z.
* **Loss:** add insertion loss (dB/in, from `IMPEDANCE_RESULT`) to the status overlay alongside Z.
* Factor a small shared helper so the router and `ComputeForTrack` share the model-selection logic rather than duplicating it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Routing a diff pair shows live **Z_diff**; single-ended nets unchanged.
- [ ] Routing a CPW-referenced trace shows CPW Z.
- [ ] Live insertion loss shown.
- [ ] No measurable routing-performance regression.

## Notes

Distinct from but related to ET4 (live length/delay gauge, <related><issue id="..." ><issue id="7f58770d-1749-4df6-a3a0-300f7c594d4e">MOON-1453</issue></issue></related>, 0.3.1). input.title: Net Inspector: insertion-loss column
input.description:
## Problem

The Net Inspector now has a model-aware average-impedance column (A5 / MOON-1430, extended in MOON-1456), but no **insertion-loss** column — even though `IMPEDANCE_CALCULATOR::ComputeForTrack()` now returns per-track conductor + dielectric loss. Loss is the metric high-speed designers most want at a glance for impedance-controlled nets.

## What needs to be upgraded

- Add `COLUMN_INSERTION_LOSS` to `pcbnew/widgets/pcb_net_inspector_panel_data_model.h` and the panel, mirroring the existing `COLUMN_AVG_IMPEDANCE` plumbing.
- In the serial impedance pass (`pcb_net_inspector_panel.cpp`, after `resultsFuture.get()`), accumulate **total** loss per net = Σ over segments of `totalLossDbPerInch() × segment-length-in-inches` (so it reflects the routed length, not just a per-inch figure), and optionally also expose dB/in.
- Format with sensible precision; sortable; blank where impedance is N/A (no stackup / non-copper).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Net Inspector shows an Insertion Loss column (total dB across the net at the board reference frequency).
- [ ] Sortable; blank for nets without a usable impedance.
- [ ] Updates when the reference frequency / roughness change (same refresh path as the impedance column).

## Notes
Optional-but-wanted completion of the loss work from MOON-1456. ~1 d.

content.text:
Four tickets created in **Zeo 0.3.0** (milestone 0.3.0), each linked to MOON-1456 with concrete upgrade specs:

| Ticket | What needs upgrading | Pri | Est |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MOON-1458** — Offset/asymmetric coupled stripline model | New numerical model (offset edge-coupled stripline, Wadell/Cohn-offset); register TAND+ROUGH for native odd-mode loss; wire real top/bot offsets into `ComputeForTrack` (drop the equivalent-single-stripline loss workaround) | High | ~3d |
| **MOON-1459** — Robust CPW/CPWG detection + native model roughness | Detect via connectivity/RTree (tracks/pads/pours, not just zones), identify true ground/ref nets, handle asymmetric gaps, tunable window; move roughness correction *inside* the coplanar model | High | ~2.5d |
| **MOON-1460** — Router diff/coplanar-aware live Z + loss | Drive coupled model from PNS in-progress pair geometry (Z_diff), run CPW detection on the head, show loss; factor shared model-selection helper | Med | ~2d |
| **MOON-1461** — Net Inspector insertion-loss column | `COLUMN_INSERTION_LOSS` mirroring the impedance column; total dB over routed length; sortable | Med | ~1d |

Each ticket states the exact files, the reference formulation/approach, and acceptance criteria (including regression checks so the current symmetric/microstrip numbers don't drift).

## Recommended implementation order
1. **MOON-1458** first — it's the deepest model change and the others lean on a correct coupled model. The key decision here is the formulation: I'd go **Wadell offset edge-coupled stripline** (well-documented closed form, validates against Polar) rather than a full field solver.
2. **MOON-1459** — independent; makes coplanar trustworthy.
3. **MOON-1461** — small, fast win once the model loss is native.
4. **MOON-1460** — router integration last, since it reuses the shared model-selection helper the others settle.

Want me to start on **MOON-1458** (the offset coupled-stripline model)? That one has a real formulation choice — I'll confirm the Wadell approach and add a `qa/` test against reference values so we can trust it. Or if you'd rather knock out the quick wins first (1461 → 1459), I can go in that order.
